guides.title: Install Veyra
guides.summary: Put Veyra on an Ubuntu server, open the setup wizard and create the first administrator.
guides.html:
Veyra runs on one Ubuntu server (or two, for high availability). The installer sets up everything it needs: the database, the web server, the telephony engine (Asterisk) and Veyra itself. You then finish in the browser with a short setup wizard.

The full technical reference is the installation document. This guide is the short version.

What you need

MinimumRecommended
Operating systemUbuntu Server 26.04 LTS or 24.04 LTS26.04 LTS, no desktop
Processor2 virtual CPUs4 or more
Memory2 GB4 to 8 GB
Disk5 GB free20 GB or more (voicemail, recordings and backups grow)
NetworkA fixed address, working DNS and time (NTP)A private address (such as 10.x or 192.168.x)

On Proxmox, use VirtIO network and disk, turn on the QEMU guest agent and use a bridged network.

On Ubuntu 24.04 the packaged Node.js is too old to build the web interface. The installer stops with a clear message if it would need it. Use 26.04, or see the installation document for the workaround.

1. Get Veyra onto the server

Sign in to the server with an account that can use sudo, then:

git clone https://github.com/manderson20/veyra.git
cd veyra

2. Check the server

sudo installer/preflight.sh

This only looks; it changes nothing. It reports blocking problems (fix them first) and warnings (read them). A common warning is that Ubuntu's installer left part of the disk unused; the installation document shows the one command that adds it.

3. Run the installer

sudo installer/install.sh

It asks before it starts. Add --dry-run to see every step without doing anything. It takes several minutes, and at the end it checks the result and prints:

  • the address of the setup wizard, such as https://192.168.1.20/setup/
  • a one-time setup token

The installer is safe to run again. If it stops half-way, fix what it reports and run it again; it carries on where it stopped and never replaces passwords, keys, certificates or data that already exist.

Things the installer never does: change SSH settings, change firewall rules, remove packages, or listen on a public internet address (unless you add --allow-public-admin).

4. Finish in the browser

  1. Open the setup address. Your browser warns about the certificate the first time; that is expected (see Certificates below).
  2. Verify access: paste the Setup token. Lost it? On the server run sudo veyra setup-token for a new one. A token works once and for 24 hours.
  3. Administrator account: your Full name, Email address and a Password of at least 12 characters. This first account is the recovery administrator: it always signs in with a password, even after you set up single sign-on.
  4. Organization: the Organization name (your school, district or company) and a Short name.
  5. Installation: an Installation name (for example District Phone System) and the Time zone.
  6. Numbering plan: the Extension length and the First extension and Last extension. You can widen it later.
  7. Review, then Finish setup. You are signed in.

The wizard also lists, on the left, what is set up after it, each with where to find it (After setup: System → Backups, for example): SIP and media addresses, outside lines, email delivery, backups, updates and high availability. Once you are signed in, Help in the top bar has a guide for each, starting with First steps after installing Veyra.

Certificates

Veyra makes its own certificate authority, so phones it sets up trust it automatically. Browsers do not, so they warn until you either:

  • install the Veyra CA certificate on the computers (download it from https://<server>/downloads/veyra-ca.crt), or
  • get a public certificate from Let's Encrypt for the server's name. See Get a public HTTPS certificate. Nothing then needs installing on computers.

Next steps

  • Turn on backups encryption and a copy to another machine.
  • Choose how updates are installed.
  • Set up email delivery under System → Settings, so alerts, voicemail and update notices can be sent.
  • Consider the firewall.

Useful console commands

CommandWhat it does
sudo installer/verify.shChecks services, HTTPS, the database and that nothing internal is exposed
sudo veyra statusA short health summary
sudo veyra setup-tokenA new setup token (before setup is finished)
sudo veyra users reset-password <email> --unlockA one-time password reset link when no administrator can sign in
sudo installer/uninstall.shRemoves Veyra but keeps the database, configuration, data and backups

When it does not work

  • "public IP address" warning in preflight: Veyra will not show its admin interface on a public address. Give the server a private address, put it behind a firewall or VPN, or use --listen <address>.
  • The web page does not open: run sudo installer/verify.sh and sudo veyra status. Another program holding port 80 or 443 is a common cause.
  • The installer stopped: read the last lines it printed (the full log is in /var/log/veyra/), fix the problem, and run sudo installer/install.sh again.

guides.title: First steps after installing Veyra
guides.summary: Finish the setup wizard, then set Veyra up in the order that gets the first phones ringing.

headings.title: 3. Set things up in this order

guides.html:
This guide takes you from a freshly installed server to the first working phones. It starts with the setup wizard, which you see only once, and then lists the order to set things up in.

Before you start

  • You need access to the server's console (the screen or an SSH session), to get the setup token.
  • Know the name of your school district, town or company, and roughly how many extensions you need.

1. Run the setup wizard

Open the server's address in a browser. As long as nobody has set Veyra up, it shows Set up Veyra. The wizard has six steps.

  1. Verify access. Paste the Setup token. The installer printed it when it finished. If you no longer have it, run sudo veyra setup-token on the server to make a new one. A token is valid for 24 hours and works once.
  2. Administrator account. Enter your Full name, Email address and a Password (at least 12 characters), twice. This account becomes the platform administrator and the recovery account. Veyra refuses passwords that contain your name or email address, use fewer than four different characters, or are a common word repeated.
  3. Organization. The Organization name is your district, town or business. The Short name is filled in from it (lower-case letters, digits and dashes). Choose it with care: it is part of every phone's SIP user name and cannot be changed later.
  4. Installation. Give this server an Installation name, such as District Phone System, and pick the Time zone. The box underneath checks the telephony engine. If it does not say the engine is running, you can still continue and check it afterwards under System → Telephony Engine.
  5. Numbering plan. Choose the Extension length (3 to 6 digits) and the First extension and Last extension. The default is 4 digits from 1000 to 7999. Extensions never start with 0 (operator), 9 (outside line), 911 or 933 (emergency).
  6. Review. Check the details and choose Finish setup. You are signed in and land on the dashboard.
The wizard also lists, on the left, what you set up after it and where: SIP and media addresses (System → Telephony Engine), Outside lines (Telephony → SIP Trunks), Email delivery (System → Settings), Backups (System → Backups), Update preferences (System → Updates) and High availability (optional) (System → High Availability), each marked After setup: with its place. The order is described below.

2. Set up your second factor

Platform administrators and organization administrators must use a second factor (an authenticator app or a passkey). By default you have 14 days to set it up. Do it now from your account page, so that you are not locked out later. See Settings: email, sign-in policy and retention for how to change this rule.

3. Set things up in this order

Each step has its own guide.

  1. Email delivery. Under System → Settings, fill in Email delivery so that Veyra can send voicemail, password reset links and alerts. See Settings: email, sign-in policy and retention.
  2. Your organization and its sites. Check the organization's details, then add a site for each campus or building, with its address and emergency caller ID. See Organizations and sites.
  3. The telephony engine. Check the SIP settings under System → Telephony Engine.
  4. Trunks and routes. Connect your carrier (SIP Trunks), then decide where incoming numbers ring (Inbound Routes) and how outside calls leave (Outbound Routes). Set up emergency calling before anyone uses the phones.
  5. Extension templates (optional). If many phones should behave the same, create a template first. See Extension templates.
  6. Users and roles. Add the people who sign in and give them roles. See Add users and give them roles.
  7. Extensions. Create an extension for each phone. See Add extensions.
  8. Deploy the changes. Changes to extensions, routes and trunks reach the phone system only when you choose Deploy changes in the top bar.
  9. Phones. Connect the desk phones under Provisioning → Devices.
  10. Backups. Turn on scheduled backups under System → Backups.

If something doesn't work

  • "Invalid setup token": the token is wrong, was already used or is older than 24 hours. Run sudo veyra setup-token on the server and paste the new one.
  • The address shows the sign-in page instead of the wizard: setup has already been completed on this server. Sign in with the administrator account.
  • "Use at least 12 characters" or another password message: choose a longer password that does not contain your name or email address.

guides.title: The dashboard
guides.summary: What the dashboard shows about the server, the phone system and today's calls.
guides.html:
The dashboard is the first page after you sign in. It shows whether Veyra and the phone system are healthy, how busy the server is, and what happened today. It refreshes by itself every 30 seconds; Refresh reloads it at once.

What you see depends on your role. Someone without the system health permission sees No dashboard access instead of the status cards.

Service status

The top row has one card each for Veyra (with its version), the Database, the Telephony engine and Modules. Each shows a status badge: normal, degraded or failed. The small text under the badge says what is wrong when something is.

Depending on what is set up, more cards follow:

  • Emergency calling: how many sites are ready for emergency calls, with a link to readiness per site and test calls.
  • Last good backup: when the last backup succeeded, and whether scheduled backups are on and encrypted. Platform administrators only.
  • High availability: the state of the cluster, when high availability is on. Platform administrators only.

Server resources

CPU, Memory, Disk and Uptime of this server. A disk that is nearly full is the most common cause of trouble, because recordings, voicemail and backups all need space.

Graphs

  • Channels: the calls going through the telephony engine, and the registered phones.
  • Calls: internal vs external: calls between your phones against calls through your carrier.
  • Phones online: phones that are registered against phones the engine knows but cannot reach.

Choose 1h, 6h, 24h or 7d above a graph for the time range. If a graph says Not available, the telephony engine is not reporting.

Calls, cluster and updates

  • Calls and registrations: the number of active calls and registered extensions right now, and the SIP trunks: how many of them are up (for example 2 of 2 up; choose it to open the trunks page), None set up, or the number with (status unknown) when the engine cannot say.
  • Cluster and updates: whether this is a standalone server or a cluster, the database role, and whether updates are available. Choose the update line to go to the Updates page.

Today and recent activity

  • Calls today: calls so far today, how many were answered and missed, and the change since the same time last week. Choose Reports for more.
  • Alerts: open alerts. Nothing is wrong means there are none.
  • Recent activity: the last changes from the audit log. Choose View audit log for all of them.

If something doesn't work

  • The telephony engine card is red: open System → Telephony Engine to see what the engine reports.
  • Graphs say Not available: the engine is not running or not reachable. Check the telephony engine card first.
  • Calls and registrations shows Not available to an organization administrator (These counts cover the whole server.): with multi-tenancy on, these counts cover every organization, so only platform administrators see them. The telephony engine is not answering. means the engine is not running or not reachable.

guides.title: Organizations and sites
guides.summary: Set up your organization's defaults, and add its sites, buildings and departments.
guides.html:
An organization is the school district, town or business Veyra serves. The setup wizard creates the first one. Everything else (extensions, users, numbers, voicemail) belongs to an organization.

A site is a campus or building of the organization. It holds the address and emergency caller ID for the phones there. A site can have buildings, for example Gym or East Wing. Departments group extensions, such as Front Office or Nurses.

Both pages are under Directory in the menu: Organizations and Sites.

Check your organization's settings

  1. Open Directory → Organizations and choose your organization.
  2. In the Details card, check or change:
    • Name and Time zone. The Short name cannot be changed.
    • Intercom: whether phones answer intercom calls on speaker. This is the default; each extension can override it.
    • Answer another phone's call: who may dial ** and an extension to answer a call ringing there: Any phone of the organization, or Only phones in the same pickup group.
    • Callers who ring through Do Not Disturb: numbers or extensions that ring every phone even when it has Do Not Disturb on, such as the district office. One per line, at most 50.
    • Outbound caller ID allow list: numbers an extension may send as caller ID besides the organization's own numbers. Changing it also needs the routing permission.
    • Hold music: what callers hear on hold.
    • Fax header and Fax station ID: printed on, and announced with, every fax the organization sends.
    • Beep when a supervisor listens in: both sides hear a beep when a supervisor starts to listen, whisper or join. Check your district's policy.
    • Users may play recordings of their own calls: off by default. Every listening is audited.
    • Active: an inactive organization is kept but cannot be used for new configuration.
  3. Choose Save changes.

Most of these settings need a deployment: choose Deploy changes in the top bar afterwards.

The organization page also has:

  • Information: the organization ID and when it was created.
  • Phone provisioning: the enrollment credential new phones use the first time they fetch their configuration. Create credential or Rotate credential; the password is shown only once.
  • Departments: choose Add department, give it a Name and, if you like, a Site. You then pick the department on each extension. My Phone layout templates can be assigned by department.

Add a site

  1. Open Directory → Sites and choose New site.
  2. Enter the Name, for example Main Campus.
  3. Time zone: leave it on The organization's to use the organization's time zone, or choose one from the list, such as America/Chicago.
  4. Emergency caller ID number: the number registered for this building with your carrier for emergency calls. It is the default for the site's extensions on 911 calls.
  5. Fill in the address: Street, City, State or region, Postal code and Country (two letters, such as US).
  6. Choose Create site.

To change a site, choose its row or Edit.

Add buildings to a site

  1. On the Sites page, choose the number in the Buildings column of the site.
  2. Choose Add building, enter the Name, and choose Add building.
  3. Leave the address empty when the building is at the site's address. Give it its own street address when it is somewhere else: emergency calls from its phones then give that address.

You then place each extension in a building on the extension's General tab, under Location.

Delete a site or building

  • A building with extensions in it cannot be deleted. Move the extensions to another building first.
  • A site with buildings cannot be deleted. Delete its buildings first.
  • When a site is deleted, its extensions, phones, profiles and paging zones keep working without a site.

More than one organization

One Veyra server can serve several organizations, for example a district and a neighboring town, with their phones kept apart. This needs multi-tenancy, which you turn on under System → Settings. See Settings: email, sign-in policy and retention.

With multi-tenancy on, choose New organization on the Organizations page (while multi-tenancy is off and one organization exists, the button is greyed out) and enter the Name, Short name and Time zone, then Create organization.

If something doesn't work

  • New organization is greyed out: multi-tenancy is off; turn it on first.
  • A warning says "Several organizations without isolation": two organizations are active but multi-tenancy is off, so their phones can reach each other. Turn multi-tenancy on.

guides.title: Add users and give them roles
guides.summary: Create accounts for the people who sign in to Veyra, give them roles, and help them when they are locked out.
guides.html:
A user is a person who signs in to Veyra: an administrator, a technician, or a staff member who checks their voicemail and changes their forwarding on My Phone. A user is not the same as an extension. You create the user here, then assign them to an extension (see Add extensions).

What a user may do depends on their roles. A user without a role can sign in but sees nothing.

If your school or company uses Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, set up single sign-on as well. People then sign in with their work account instead of a Veyra password.

The roles

RoleWhat it is for
Platform AdministratorFull control of this Veyra installation and every organization on it.
Organization AdministratorManages users, telephony and devices within an organization.
Site AdministratorManages extensions and devices at a site.
TechnicianMaintains devices and views telephony configuration.
Standard UserSelf-service access to their own phone and voicemail.
Read-Only UserCan view, but not change, configuration.

Every role except Platform Administrator is given for one organization. Only a platform administrator can give the Platform Administrator role.

The Assign role dialog gives every role for a whole organization, including Site Administrator. It does not yet offer to limit a role to one site.

Add a user

  1. Open Directory → Users and choose New user.
  2. Enter the Full name and Email address. The email address is what they sign in with.
  3. Enter an Initial password of at least 12 characters. It is temporary: the user must choose their own at the first sign-in. Give it to them over a channel you trust.
  4. Choose the Organization. A platform administrator can leave it empty for a platform-level account.
  5. Choose Create user. Veyra opens the new user's page.
  6. Under Roles, choose Assign role. Pick the Role and the Organization, then Assign role.

Veyra may ask for your password again before it assigns a role. This protects against someone using a computer you left signed in.

Veyra refuses passwords that contain the person's name or email address, have fewer than four different characters, or are a common word repeated.

The user's page

Choose a user in the list to open their page.

  • Profile: change the Full name or Email address, or switch Account enabled off. Disabling an account signs the person out everywhere; you cannot disable your own.
  • Changing an email address: it is what the person signs in with from then on. Veyra asks you to sign in again if you have not recently, signs them out, cancels any password reset link, and emails their old address if email delivery is set up. An account that signs in through an identity provider gets its address from there, and cannot be changed here. An account that also works in an organization you do not administer needs a platform administrator.
  • Deleting a user: switch off Account enabled and save, then choose Delete user. The account, its roles and its personal settings (My Phone layout, contacts) are removed for good. Their phones stay, unassigned, with their voicemail; recordings and call history stay; the audit log keeps their name and address. You cannot delete yourself or the recovery administrator. If they had a phone, deploy changes afterwards.
  • Account: the sign-in method, the last sign-in, the password's state, whether two-factor sign-in is on, and whether the account is locked.
  • Roles: the roles the user holds. Use the bin icon to remove one. At least one platform administrator must remain.
  • Sign-in: accounts at sign-in providers (single sign-on) linked to this user. Unlink removes the link.
  • Active sessions: where the account is signed in. Sign out everywhere ends them all without changing the password.
  • Connected apps (Companion): browsers where the person signed in to the Companion extension.

When someone is locked out

They forgot their password. Choose Reset password at the top of their page. Then pick one:

  • Create a one-time reset link (recommended). Veyra shows a link that works once and expires. Choose Copy link and send it to the person. The link is shown only once.
  • Set a password now. Enter a New password. It is temporary unless you switch on Permanent password.

Either way the person is signed out everywhere and any lockout is cleared. People can also use Forgot password on the sign-in page themselves, if email delivery is set up.

Their account is locked after too many failed sign-ins. The Account card says Locked until a certain time. Choose Unlock now.

They lost the phone with their authenticator app. Next to Two-factor, choose Reset, then Reset two-factor. Their authenticator devices and recovery codes are removed and they are signed out. They set up a new one at their next sign-in.

You cannot reset your own password or second factor here. Use your account page. If the last platform administrator loses their second factor, run veyra users mfa-reset on the server.

If something doesn't work

  • "A user with this email address already exists": each email address can belong to only one user. Search the list for it; the account may be disabled.
  • The user signs in but sees nothing: they have no role. Assign one.
  • "Choose the user's organization": only a platform administrator can create a user without an organization.
  • You cannot see the Roles card or the Assign role button: your own role does not include managing roles. Ask an organization or platform administrator.

guides.title: Add extensions
guides.summary: Create an extension for each phone, assign it to a person, and set its caller ID, location, voicemail and phone options.
guides.html:
An extension is a number that a phone registers with, such as 1204. It can belong to a person, or be a shared phone (a classroom, the front desk, a lobby phone). Each extension has a SIP user name and secret that the phone uses to connect.

The extensions are under Telephony → Extensions.

Before you start

  • Check the Numbering plan card at the bottom of the Extensions page: the extension length and the range new numbers come from.
  • Add your sites and buildings first, so you can place each phone (see Organizations and sites).
  • Create the users who will have their own phone (see Add users and give them roles).

Create an extension

  1. Open Telephony → Extensions and choose New extension.
  2. The Extension number is already filled in with the next free number. Type another, or choose Suggest next free.
  3. Enter a Name, for example Front Office or Jane Doe.
  4. Pick the Assigned user (optional), or leave it at Shared phone (no user). Only active users of the same organization are listed. Picking a user fills in the name if it is empty. When there are many users, type part of a name or email in Find a user to narrow the list.
    • Template (optional): shown once the organization has an extension template. The template's settings apply to the new extension, and the settings it locks stay as the template has them. Leave No template for none.
  5. If you like, fill in the Caller ID name and Caller ID number that colleagues see. They default to the name and the extension number.
  6. Emergency caller ID number: the building's number registered for emergency calls. Leave it empty to use the site's or the emergency route's number.
  7. Choose the Site, Building, Location (dispatchable) (such as Room 101, first floor) and Department. The site and building decide the address given on emergency calls; the location tells responders the room.
  8. Leave Enabled on and choose Create extension.
  9. Choose Deploy changes in the top bar. Until then the phone system does not know the new extension.

The number must have the plan's length, lie within its range, and not start with a reserved digit. It must also be free in the organization: extensions, ring groups and queues share one set of numbers.

The extension's page

Choose an extension in the list to open it. The tabs across the top are:

General

  • Details: change the Extension number, Name, Assigned user or Enabled. Changing the number also changes the SIP user name, so the phone must be set up again.
  • Information: the SIP user name (the organization's short name and the number, such as lincoln-1204), whether a secret is set, the class of service, and when it changed.
  • Location: the site, building, dispatchable location and department.

Caller ID

  • Caller ID name and Caller ID number: what colleagues see on internal calls.
  • Outbound caller ID number: sent to the carrier on outside calls. It must be one of the organization's numbers (from its inbound routes) or on the organization's allow list. Empty: the route's or the trunk's number is used.
  • Outbound caller ID name: sent with it; carriers may replace it.
  • Emergency caller ID number: sent on 911 calls instead of the regular caller ID.

Call handling

  • Call handling: Do Not Disturb, Callers who still ring during Do Not Disturb, Call waiting, Refuse callers who hide their number, the four forwards (all calls, when busy, when unanswered, when the phone is offline) and the Ring time (seconds) before voicemail or the no-answer forward. These take effect at once, except the ring time, which needs a deployment. Choose Save call handling.
  • Restrictions: the Extension template the extension follows (shown once a template exists), the Class of service (which outside routes and feature codes it may use) and Intercom (whether other phones can call it on speaker). Settings locked by a template cannot be changed here. See Extension templates.

The person can change their own forwarding and Do Not Disturb on My Phone or with the feature codes. See Feature codes people can dial.

Follow me

Rings other numbers, such as a mobile, as well as the desk phone. Add up to 10 numbers with Add a number, choose whether they ring All at once or One after another, and choose Save follow me. Then switch Follow me on. Outside numbers must press 1 to accept stops a mobile's voicemail from taking the call.

Voicemail

Shows the extension's voicemail box. Without a box, unanswered calls simply end. Choose Create box (or Edit box) to set:

  • the PIN (4 to 10 digits; leave it empty for a random one, shown once),
  • the Ring time (seconds) before voicemail answers,
  • the Operator extension (press 0),
  • the email for new messages: Use the extension user's email address, or another address, with Attach the recording to the email and Delete the message from the box once it has been emailed,
  • Delete messages older than (days).

From the phone, the person dials *97 for their greeting and messages. Email needs email delivery to be set up under System → Settings.

Phones

  • Registered phones: the phones connected as this extension right now, with their address, model and whether they are reachable.
  • Phones that may register: how many phones may use this extension at once, 1 to 16. Empty means as many as are provisioned with it. Raise it to let a softphone register beside the desk phone.
  • Hotline number: lifting the handset dials this number at once. Use it for elevator, lobby, door and emergency phones. With Warm-line delay (seconds) above 0, the phone first waits that long for a digit.
  • Fax machine (T.38): switch it on when a fax machine is plugged into an ATA port for this extension, and your trunk supports T.38. Off, the fax travels as audio, which works with any trunk. Set the ATA's fax mode to match.
  • Phones: the provisioned devices carrying this extension, as line 1 or as an extra line.

The hotline, phone count and T.38 setting need a deployment.

Groups

The ring groups, call queues and pickup groups the extension belongs to.

Credentials

The User name and Secret the phone registers with. Show secret reveals it (this is recorded in the audit log). New secret replaces it: the phone stops registering until it gets the new secret and you deploy.

Delete an extension

Choose Delete at the top of the extension's page and type the extension number to confirm. The phone stops working at the next deployment.

Change the numbering plan

People who can change system settings see a form in the Numbering plan card on the Extensions page: Extension length, First extension, Last extension and Reserved leading digits (keep 0, 9, 911 and 933). Choose Save plan. Existing extensions keep their numbers; the plan applies to new and renumbered ones. The numbering plan is shared by every organization on the server.

If something doesn't work

  • "Changes not yet deployed": choose Deploy changes in the top bar.
  • "Installation key missing": Veyra cannot store or show SIP secrets. Run sudo veyra installation-key check on the server.
  • A No secret badge: choose New secret on the Credentials tab.
  • The phone does not register: check the user name and secret on the phone against the Credentials tab, and that you deployed. The Registers from column shows where a phone connects from; behind NAT means it is behind a router.
  • "Extensions are numbered from … to …" or "Numbers starting with … are reserved": pick a number inside the plan's range.
  • "Number in use": an extension, ring group or queue already has that number.
  • "The user belongs to a different organization": a user can only be assigned to an extension of their own organization.

guides.title: Extension templates
guides.summary: Give many extensions the same settings at once, and lock the ones people should not change.
guides.html:
An extension template is one set of settings that many extensions follow, for example Classroom phones or Office staff. When you change the template, you apply it again and every extension that follows it gets the new settings.

A template can also lock a setting. A locked setting cannot be changed on the extension while it follows the template.

The templates are under Telephony → Extension Templates.

What a template can set

SettingWhat it does
Class of serviceWhich outside routes and feature codes the phones may use
IntercomWhether other phones can call them on speaker
Phones that may registerHow many phones may use each extension at once (1 to 16)
DepartmentThe department the extensions are in
Ring time (seconds)How long they ring before voicemail or the no-answer forward (5 to 120)
Call waitingSwitch call waiting off
Callers who hide their numberRefuse outside callers without caller ID
Outside caller ID number and nameWhat the carrier is sent on outside calls
Forward when busy, Forward when not answered, Forward when the phone is offlineWhere those calls go
Attach the recording to the emailFor the extension's own voicemail box
Delete after emailDelete voicemail once it has been emailed
Delete messages older than (days)1 to 3650
Operator extension (0 in voicemail)Where a caller goes when pressing 0 in voicemail

Anything the template does not set stays as each extension has it.

Create a template

  1. Open Telephony → Extension Templates and choose New template.
  2. Enter a Name and, if you like, a Description.
  3. Tick each setting the template should set, and fill in its value.
  4. Tick Locked next to a setting to stop it being changed on the extensions.
  5. Choose Create template.

Put extensions on a template

Open an extension, go to the Call handling tab, and pick the template under Extension template in the Restrictions card. Choose Save changes. All the template's settings are applied when you save.

Apply a changed template

After editing a template, its extensions keep their old values until you apply it.

  1. On the templates page, choose Apply… next to the template.
  2. Veyra lists each extension that differs from the template, with every change (for example Ring time: 20 → 30).
  3. Choose Apply to … extensions.

Some settings, such as the ring time and intercom, reach the phone system only at the next deployment. Choose Deploy changes in the top bar when Veyra asks.

Delete a template

Choose the bin icon next to the template. Its extensions keep their current settings and stop following it; nothing is locked any more.

If something doesn't work

  • "Set by the template" when saving an extension: that setting is locked by the extension's template. Change the template instead, or unlock the setting there.
  • The Extension template field is missing on an extension: no template exists in its organization yet.
  • Apply… is greyed out: no extension follows this template yet.

guides.title: Feature codes people can dial
guides.summary: The star codes phones dial to forward calls, turn on Do Not Disturb, pick up calls and more, and how to change them.

headings.title: Load the codes from your old phone system

guides.html:
Feature codes are what people dial on their phone to change its settings or reach a feature, such as *72 to forward their calls. The codes start with * or #, so they never clash with extension numbers.

The page is under Telephony → Feature Codes. It shows each code with its Default, and whether it is Enabled. Veyra's defaults follow FreePBX, so people moving from a FreePBX system keep their habits.

The codes

These are the defaults. Your installation may have changed some of them: the page shows the codes in use.

DefaultFeatureHow to use it
*78Do Not Disturb onCallers hear busy, or the busy greeting.
*79Do Not Disturb offThe phone rings again.
*76Do Not Disturb toggleA phone key on this code lights while Do Not Disturb is on.
*72Forward all callsDial with the number, or alone and enter it.
*73Forward all calls off
*90Forward on busyDial with the number, or alone and enter it.
*91Forward on busy off
*52Forward on no answerDial with the number, or alone and enter it.
*53Forward on no answer off
*21Find me / follow me toggle
*80IntercomDial with the extension: that phone answers on speaker.
*Direct to voicemailDial with an extension, or transfer to it: straight to its greeting.
*28Call flow toggleFollowed by the flow's index: switches it between its two destinations.
*27Time condition overrideFollowed by the condition's index: forces the opposite state until the schedule changes. Dial again to clear it.
*30Block a callerEnter a number; it is refused for the whole organization.
*31Unblock a callerEnter a number to remove it.
*32Block the last callerBlocks the last outside number that rang this phone directly.
*45Queue log in / log outAlone: every queue this phone may join. With a queue number: that queue only.
*46Queue pause / unpauseAlone or with a queue number.
*47Queue waiting countWith a queue number: says how many callers are waiting.
*1Record this callDuring a call: starts recording (a beep); again, stops it.
*2Attended transferDuring a call, then the number: talk first, hang up to connect.
##Blind transferDuring a call, then the number: the call goes straight across.
*36Colleague's presenceWith an extension, on a phone key: shows that colleague's presence; pressing it calls them.
*37Set your presenceFollowed by 1 available, 2 away, 3 busy, 4 in a meeting, 5 at lunch, 6 out. Alone: back to available.
*85Pick up a parked callFollowed by the parking slot number.
*67Hide your number on one callFollowed by the number. Emergency calls always show it.
*69Call back the last callerCalls the last outside number that rang this phone directly.
*70Call waiting off for one callFollowed by the number.
*77Refuse callers who hide their number
*87Accept callers who hide their number
*222Listen to a call (supervisor)With an extension: hear its call without being heard.
*223Whisper on a call (supervisor)With an extension: only that phone's user hears you.
*224Join a call (supervisor)With an extension: both sides hear you.

The supervisor codes work only on phones whose class of service allows supervising. The class of service of an extension can also block other codes.

Codes that never change

The Always available card lists the codes every installation has:

CodeFeature
*97Your own voicemail
*98Any voicemail box
*8Pick up a call ringing in your pickup group
** and an extensionPick up the call ringing on that phone
*43Echo test
*60Speaking clock
*95Record a prompt

Change a code

You need the permission to change routing.

  1. Type the new code in the Code column. A code starts with * or # and has 1 to 7 characters (digits, * or #).
  2. To turn a feature off entirely, switch Enabled off.
  3. Choose Save at the top of the page.
  4. Choose Deploy changes in the top bar. The new codes work after the deployment.

Tell staff about the change, and update any phone keys that use the old code.

Load the codes from your old phone system

If staff are used to the codes of another system, use Code sets:

  1. Under Load a code set, pick the set, for example Metaswitch (Sparklight code card).
  2. Veyra puts its codes into the table, but does not save them yet. The box underneath lists every change and any differences the set cannot remove.
  3. Check the table, then choose Save and deploy.

If something doesn't work

  • "… is already used": the code belongs to one of the fixed codes, or starts with **. Pick another.
  • "… is also used by …": two enabled features cannot share a code.
  • A code does nothing on the phone: check that it is enabled, that you deployed, and that the extension's class of service allows it.

guides.title: Settings: email, sign-in policy and retention
guides.summary: Set up email delivery, the two-factor rule, how long data is kept, the installation key and multi-tenancy.
guides.html:
System → Settings holds the settings that apply to the whole server. Everyone sees the Installation card (name, version, deployment, whether multi-tenancy and central management are on) and Appearance, where you choose a light, dark or automatic theme for your own browser. The other cards appear only to administrators who may see system settings; some are for platform administrators only.

The HTTPS certificate card and the Companion settings on the same page have their own guides.

The Elsewhere card points to settings kept on other pages: SIP and media addresses on System → Telephony Engine, backups on System → Backups, single sign-on on System → Sign-in, and the Companion rollout on System → Companion rollout.

Email delivery

Veyra sends all its email through your mail server: voicemail and fax, password reset links, alerts, reports, and update and emergency notices. Until this is set up, nothing is emailed; with Send email off, Veyra sends no email at all and voicemail stays in the boxes.

  1. Switch on Send email.
  2. Enter the SMTP server (for example smtp.office365.com or smtp-relay.gmail.com) and the Port.
  3. Choose the Connection security: STARTTLS (usually port 587) or TLS from the start (usually port 465). None is allowed only for a relay on the server itself.
  4. If the server needs a sign-in, enter the User name and Password. Leave the user name empty for no sign-in. The password is stored encrypted and never shown again; to keep it, leave the field empty.
  5. Enter the From address and From name. Many mail servers only accept their own domain as the sender.
  6. Choose Save settings.
  7. Choose Send me a test message. Veyra sends it to your own account's email address and shows whether the server accepted it.

The line under the form shows the Queue: messages waiting to be sent, and messages given up on after a day of retries. Each one given up on is in the audit log as mail.failed.

With Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, the simplest choice is often their SMTP relay service with the Veyra server's address allowed, so no password is needed.

Two-factor policy

Decides who must use a second factor when signing in to Veyra.

  • Required for: tick the roles that must use one. By default these are Platform Administrator and Organization Administrator.
  • Allowed second factors: Passkeys (Touch ID, Windows Hello, a security key or a phone; needs the server's name and a trusted certificate) and Authenticator apps (six-digit codes). At least one must stay ticked.
  • Days to set it up: after their first sign-in with such a role, people can sign in without a second factor for this many days (0 to 365; default 14). 0 means they must set it up at once.
  • Trust a browser for (days): people may tick Trust this browser and then sign in there with just the password for this many days (0 to 90). 0 turns it off.

Choose Save policy. Affected people are told at their next sign-in.

The recovery administrator is not exempt. If they lose their second factor, run veyra users mfa-reset on the server. People who sign in with single sign-on use their provider's second factor instead.

Retention

Platform administrators decide how long Veyra keeps each kind of data. The table shows each kind with its days, how many rows it has, its size, and its oldest entry.

DataDefault (days)Lowest allowed
Audit log730365
Call history40030
Alert history36530
Update history73090
Cluster events73090
Firewall events and expired bans907
Provisioning request log307
Page log907
Faxes907
Packet captures71
Engine metrics samples142
Central console samples307

To change it, type the days in Keep (days) and choose Save. Going below 30 days asks you to type SHORTEN to confirm. Old data is removed once a day; Apply now removes it at once. Removed data can only be recovered from a backup.

Voicemail messages are kept per box (on the extension's Voicemail tab), not here.

Installation key

The installation key encrypts the stored secrets: SIP passwords, the SMTP password, two-factor secrets and recordings. The card shows its Fingerprint and the result of the last rotation.

To replace it, choose Rotate the key…, then Rotate now. Veyra makes a new key and re-encrypts every secret with it. The web interface and the worker restart, which takes under a minute; calls are not affected. Afterwards take a backup, and remove the previous key file from the server once the backup is verified.

Multi-tenancy

Multi-tenancy lets one Veyra server serve several organizations whose phones cannot reach each other. The card shows whether it is On or Off, how many organizations are active, and what every organization shares (trunks, the numbering plan, the mail server, the firewall, updates, modules and sign-in providers).

  • Turn on: choose Turn on, then Run checks and turn on. Veyra first builds the configuration with a test copy of your organization and proves that neither can reach the other's phones, voicemail or queues. Your current organization and its phones do not change. Then you can add organizations (see Organizations and sites).
  • Turn off: only possible while a single organization is active.

If something doesn't work

  • The test message fails: read the message Veyra shows. Check the server name, port and security together (587 with STARTTLS, or 465 with TLS), and the user name and password. Check that the mail server accepts the From address.
  • "Unencrypted delivery … is only allowed to a loopback relay": choose STARTTLS or TLS.
  • "Enter the password for the SMTP user name": a user name needs a password.
  • The card says Needs attention: the saved settings have a problem; it is shown in the yellow box.
  • Turning on multi-tenancy fails: the list under the card shows which check failed.

guides.title: Connect phones to Veyra
guides.summary: How a new phone finds this server, signs in for its configuration, and learns to trust Veyra's certificate.

headings.title: See what a phone asked for

guides.html:
Every phone, adapter and speaker that Veyra manages downloads its configuration from Veyra. Nobody types settings into the phone. You do three things once, and after that each new phone sets itself up when it is plugged in:

  1. Tell the phones where Veyra is (the provisioning URL).
  2. Give new phones a password to sign in with the first time (the enrollment credential).
  3. Make the phones trust Veyra's HTTPS certificate.

Then you register each phone by its MAC address. See Add a phone.

The provisioning URL

Phones download their files from https://<your Veyra server>/provisioning/. You can copy this address in two places:

  • Provisioning → Templates, in the Redirect services card (Provisioning URL).
  • On the organization's page under Directory → Organizations, in the Phone provisioning card (Server URL).

The enrollment credential

A new phone signs in with its organization's enrollment credential the first time. Veyra then gives each phone its own user name and password in its configuration, so from then on every phone signs in on its own. The device page shows that user name on the Status tab as Credential user (it looks like dev-0004f2abcdef).

To create the credential:

  1. Open Directory → Organizations and open the organization.
  2. In the Phone provisioning card, choose Create credential and confirm.
  3. Copy the Password right away. It is shown only once.

The user name is veyra- followed by the organization's short name.

Rotate credential makes a new password. Phones that already have their configuration keep working, because they use their own password. Only phones that have not finished their first download need the new one.

How the phone finds Veyra

Pick one of these. You only need it for new or factory-reset phones, because a configured phone remembers the address.

  • DHCP option 66. On the DHCP scope of the voice network, set option 66 to the provisioning URL. Poly phones also read option 160. You can put the credential in the address so nothing is typed on the phone: https://veyra-yourorg:PASSWORD@pbx.example.org/provisioning/.
  • Typed on the phone. In the phone's own menu or web page, set the provisioning server type to HTTPS, the server to the address without https://, and the enrollment user name and password.
  • The vendor's redirect service. Some brands ask the vendor's cloud where to go the first time they start. The Redirect services card on Provisioning → Templates lists them:
BrandServiceWhat to do
YealinkYealink RPSAdd the MAC addresses in the RPS portal with the provisioning URL as the server.
PolyPoly ZTP in Poly LensRegister the MAC addresses with the provisioning URL, or use DHCP option 160.
GrandstreamGrandstream GDMSImport the MAC addresses with the provisioning URL as the config server.
AlgoNoneUse DHCP option 66, or set the server once in the device's web page.

Each brand has an Export … MACs button, for example Export Yealink MACs. It downloads a CSV of the phones you have registered for that brand, with the MAC address in both forms and the provisioning URL, ready to import into the vendor's portal.

Making phones trust Veyra

Veyra's HTTPS certificate is signed by Veyra's own certificate authority (the Veyra CA). Phones only trust the big public certificate authorities, so a new phone refuses Veyra's certificate. There are three ways around this.

A public certificate. If the server has a public certificate (for example from Let's Encrypt) for the address the phones use, phones trust it already. Nothing more to do.

The trust bootstrap (Poly and Yealink). Over plain HTTP, Veyra hands a new phone only public information: the Veyra CA certificate and the HTTPS address. The phone installs the certificate, restarts, and downloads everything else, including its SIP password, over HTTPS. To use it:

  1. Whoever runs the server sets VEYRA_PROVISIONING_HTTP=1 in /etc/veyra/installer.conf and runs the installer again. Until then, Veyra does not answer plain HTTP at all.
  2. Point DHCP option 66 (and 160 for Poly) on the staging or voice network at the http address: http://<your Veyra server>/provisioning/.
  3. Check which networks may use the bootstrap: System → Firewall, card Phone bootstrap networks. Left empty, it uses the local networks from the SIP settings. Phones on any other network are refused.
  4. Plug the phone in. It restarts once after the bootstrap. Its Status tab then shows Trusted, HTTPS under Trust.

When the bootstrap is on, the Phone provisioning card also shows the switch Include the enrollment credential in the bootstrap. Turned on, new phones get the credential from the bootstrap and nothing has to be typed. Anyone on that network can read it, though, so use it only on a separate staging network and rotate the credential after each batch of phones.

Once a phone has downloaded its configuration over HTTPS, Veyra refuses to send it the plain-HTTP bootstrap again. This stops someone from tricking it back onto HTTP. If you factory-reset the phone, open its device page, go to the Status tab and choose Allow bootstrap again.

Grandstream and Algo. These devices do not get the HTTP bootstrap. Point them straight at the https address. If a device refuses the certificate, download it from https://<your Veyra server>/downloads/veyra-ca.crt and add it in the device's web page as a trusted certificate. Grandstream's configuration from Veyra installs the Veyra CA by itself (setting install_ca) and leaves certificate checking off. Once the CA is installed you can turn checking on with the setting validate_server_certificate (see Device profiles).

Whoever runs the server can set VEYRA_PROVISIONING_HTTP_MODE=full so that every file, SIP passwords included, is also sent over plain HTTP. Use it only for phones that cannot take the certificate any other way. The Phone provisioning card shows a warning while it is on.

See what a phone asked for

Provisioning → Requests lists every configuration request for 30 days: the time, the phone's MAC and network address, the file, the result with its reason, and the phone's software. Tick Problems only to see just the refused requests, or search for a MAC or address.

  • No row at all means the phone is not reaching this server: check the provisioning URL it was given.
  • Wrong sign-in means its credential is missing or wrong.
  • Unknown phone means no device has that MAC address yet.
  • No such file is usually harmless, because phones ask for optional files.

A phone Veyra does not know belongs to no organization yet, so only platform administrators see its requests.

If something doesn't work

Open Provisioning → Devices. What you see there tells you how far the phone got.

  • The phone appears under "Phones seen but not registered". It reached Veyra and signed in correctly, but nobody has registered its MAC address yet. Choose Register on its row. This list covers the last 7 days.
  • The phone is in neither list. Veyra never saw a correct sign-in from it. Check:
    • the address on the phone or in DHCP (including /provisioning/ at the end, and https or http);
    • the enrollment user name and password (rotate the credential if you are not sure, and use the new one);
    • that the phone can reach the server, and that the firewall lets it in;
    • the certificate. A Poly or Yealink phone that cannot use HTTPS yet needs the trust bootstrap, a public certificate, or the CA installed by hand. A phone using the bootstrap must be on one of the Phone bootstrap networks.
  • The phone is registered but its status is "Never provisioned". The phone has not asked for its files since you registered it. Restart it, or wait for its daily check.
  • Status "Error". The last request failed. Open the phone, go to the Configuration tab and choose Render. An error there (for example a missing template) is the reason. Also read the Needs attention box at the top of the page.
  • A reset phone no longer gets the bootstrap. Use Allow bootstrap again on its Status tab.
  • A phone that worked is refused. Check that Enabled is on in the device's settings. Disabled phones are refused their configuration.

Every official template is marked experimental for now. They follow the vendors' documentation but have not yet been checked on real hardware. Paging speakers, horns and adapters

  • Line 1 registers as the device's page extension. Line 2, if you add one, is its ring extension.
  • The paging zones the profile Receives become the device's multicast listening zones. The template setting multicast_format chooses which pages it hears: rtp (plain multicast, the default), poly (Poly group paging) or both.

Families and models

Templates come in two kinds:

  • A base template (shown as Base template in the list) holds the settings a whole family shares, such as Poly VVX (common settings) or Yealink (common settings). A device profile can point at it, and then serves every model of the family.
  • A model template serves the models it lists and inherits everything else from its base template.

Which you choose in a profile is explained in Device profiles.

Firmware the templates expect

Each template's page (Overview tab, Firmware) names the firmware it was written for, for example UC Software 5.9 / 6.x for the VVX or Yealink firmware 66.86 / 96.86 and later. Older firmware may ignore some settings. To update phones from Veyra, see Phone firmware.

A device that is not listed

  • A model that is not listed cannot be served by an official template, even when its family is. A profile for that family shows the problem No template under … supports model ….
  • You can make your own template, or import one someone else made. See Customize a provisioning template.

How phones first reach Veyra

The Redirect services card on the same page shows the provisioning URL and each vendor's zero-touch service. See Connect phones to Veyra.

guides.title: Add a phone
guides.summary: Register a phone by its MAC address, give it a profile and extensions, and check that it picked up its configuration.
guides.html:
Veyra knows each phone by its MAC address, the hardware address printed on the label under the phone and on its box. When a phone asks for its configuration, Veyra looks up the MAC address, takes the phone's device profile and extension, and builds the files for that exact model.

Before you start

  • The phones must know how to reach Veyra. See Connect phones to Veyra.
  • Create a device profile for this kind of phone first. See Device profiles.
  • Create the extension the phone will use (under Telephony → Extensions).

Register a phone

  1. Open Provisioning → Devices and choose Register a phone.
  2. Fill in the form:
    • Organization: shown only if you manage more than one.
    • MAC address (required): from the phone's label. Colons or dashes are optional, so 00:04:f2:ab:cd:ef and 0004F2ABCDEF are both fine. Each MAC address can be registered only once.
    • Manufacturer and Model (required): the list shows the models Veyra has templates for. Pick the exact model, because the model decides which template is used.
    • Label: a name you will recognize, such as Room 112.
    • Device profile: the profile with the settings and keys for this phone. Without a profile, nothing is sent to the phone.
    • Extension (line 1): the extension the phone registers as. Without it, the phone gets its configuration but does not register.
    • Site: leave it on From the profile to use the profile's site. The site sets the phone's time zone.
    • Location (dispatchable): the floor and room, used for emergency calls from this phone. It wins over the extension's location. You can change it later on the phone's page.
  3. Choose Register phone.

The phone gets its configuration the next time it checks in. To make it check now, restart it, or use Reprovision on its page (see below).

Register a phone that has already called in

If a phone reaches Veyra and signs in with the enrollment credential before you register it, it appears in the card Phones seen but not registered at the top of the Devices page. The card shows its MAC address, the model it reported, its network address and when it was last seen (phones from the last 7 days).

Choose Register on its row. The MAC address, manufacturer, model and organization are filled in for you. Choose the profile and extension and register it as above.

The phone's page

Click a phone in the list to open it. The list can be searched by label, MAC address, model or extension number, and filtered by profile.

Settings tab

Here you change everything from the registration form, and also:

  • Building: the building the phone is in. The list shows the buildings of the phone's site; No building leaves it unset.
  • Extra lines: Add line gives the phone a second, third… extension, up to 8 lines in all. Each extension can appear only once on a phone. On an analog adapter, each line is one phone port (see Analog adapters and fax machines).
  • Firmware override: a firmware image for this phone only. Left on From the profile, the phone gets the profile's firmware. See Phone firmware.
  • Setting overrides: the template's settings for this phone only. A blank field keeps the profile's value, which is shown greyed in the field. A yes/no setting is a list: As the profile (which shows the profile's value), Yes or No. Secret settings, such as passwords, are shown as dots.
  • Enabled: a disabled phone is refused its configuration until you turn it back on.

Choose Save changes. The phone takes the change at its next check, or right away if you choose Reprovision.

Changing the Device profile clears this phone's setting overrides, because they belong to the old template.

Line keys tab

By default the phone uses its profile's keys. Tick Override the profile's keys for this phone to give this phone its own key list. See Phone keys.

Configuration tab

Choose Render to see the exact files the phone downloads, built now, with passwords masked. Use it to check a change before the phone gets it. If a template setting or key uses a provisioning variable that nobody has defined, a Missing variables box lists it.

The Variables card lists the provisioning variables that reach this phone and where each comes from (Installation, Organization, Site or Profile). See Provisioning variables.

Status tab

  • Provisioning: the status, the last request and its result, the address it came from, what the phone reports about itself, the template used, the phone's own Credential user, and Trust (whether it has switched to HTTPS).
  • Firmware: the version assigned, the version the phone is running, and whether it is Up to date or has an Update pending.

Buttons at the top

  • Reprovision: asks the phone to download its configuration again now.
  • Reboot: asks the phone to restart.
  • Delete: removes the phone from Veyra. The phone keeps its last configuration until it is reset, but its own provisioning password stops working.

Reprovision and Reboot send a message to the phone over its line 1 registration. They work only when the phone has an extension and is registered right now.

What the status means

StatusMeaning
Never provisionedThe phone has not downloaded anything since it was registered.
ProvisionedThe last request worked.
Not seen latelyThe phone has not checked in for 48 hours. Phones check once a day, so it may be off or unplugged.
ErrorThe last request failed. Look at the Configuration tab and the Needs attention box.

The Needs attention box at the top of a phone's page lists problems such as:

  • No profile: nothing is served to this phone. Choose a profile.
  • No extension: the phone will not register. Choose an Extension (line 1).
  • No template under … supports model … The profile's template family has no template for this model. Check the model, or pick another profile.
  • The extension of line 1 no longer exists. Choose another extension.

If something doesn't work

  • The phone does not pick up its configuration. Work through If something doesn't work in Connect phones to Veyra.
  • The phone downloaded its files but does not register. Check that it has an Extension (line 1), then look at Telephony → Registrations (see See which phones are registered). If more phones share the extension than it allows, the last phone to register pushes out the earliest.
  • "A device with that MAC address is already registered." Search the Devices list for the MAC address. If you cannot find it, it is registered in an organization you cannot see; ask an administrator of that organization.
  • A change does not show on the phone. Choose Reprovision. If the phone is not registered, restart it by hand.

guides.title: Device profiles
guides.summary: Group phones that share a template, settings, keys, paging zones and firmware, for example one profile per building.
guides.html:
A device profile holds everything that phones of one kind share: the template, the settings, the line keys, the paging zones and the firmware. Each phone points at one profile. Change the profile once and every phone using it follows.

A good rule: one profile per kind of phone and per building, for example VVX, Building A and VVX, Building B. The two differ only in their paging zones and maybe a few keys. Provisioning variables can often replace such near-copies: one profile, with a value that differs per site.

Create a profile

  1. Open Provisioning → Device Profiles and choose New profile.
  2. Fill in:
    • Organization: shown only if you manage more than one.
    • Name (required): unique within the organization, for example VVX, Building A.
    • Site (optional): the building these phones are in. Phones registered with this profile take this site unless you choose another. The site sets the phones' time zone and the site's provisioning variables.
    • Template (required): choose a family or a single model:
      • A family (listed as Manufacturer — Name (family)) serves every model under it. One "Poly VVX" profile can hold VVX 411 and VVX 450 phones together. Veyra picks the right template for each phone's model.
      • A model template serves only the models listed next to it.
    • Description: for your own notes.
    • Firmware: the firmware image the phones should run. Leave Keep the phones' current firmware if Veyra should not manage it. Only images for the template's manufacturer are listed. See Phone firmware.
  3. Fill in the settings, line keys and paging zones (below).
  4. Choose Create profile.

Then register phones against it on the Devices page (see Add a phone).

Settings

Once you choose a template, the Settings heading lists the settings that template offers, such as the SIP transport, how often the phone checks for changes, an administrator password for the phone's own menus, or the screen saver. Each field shows the template's default greyed; leave it empty to keep the default. Yes/no settings are tick boxes. A password setting is never shown again once saved: the field shows dots, and typing replaces it. The name under each field (for example polling_hour) is the setting's name in the template.

What the settings mean depends on the template. You can read their descriptions and defaults on the template's Variables tab under Provisioning → Templates.

Changing a profile's template clears its settings, because the new template has different ones.

A single phone can override any of these on its own page (Setting overrides).

Line keys

The keys every phone of the profile gets, in order. See Phone keys for each key type, open slots that users fill themselves, and per-phone overrides.

Paging zones

The Paging zones heading lists the paging zones of the organization (they are made under Telephony → Paging Zones). For each zone the phones should take part in:

  1. Tick the zone.
  2. Choose what the phones do:
    • Receive: the phones play pages sent to this zone.
    • Send: the phones may page this zone.
  3. Optionally give the zone a role: Default group, Priority group or Emergency group. Each role can be given to only one zone in a profile. On Poly phones, the default group is the one the phone's paging button uses, and priority and emergency pages interrupt calls.

A profile can take part in up to 25 zones. A phone cannot change its zones on its own: to give one phone different zones, give it a different profile.

The profile's page

Click a profile in the list to open it. Besides the same form, it shows:

  • Models served: each model the profile can serve and the exact template it uses. Click a template to open it.
  • Information: how many phones use the profile (view lists them), its firmware, and when it was created and changed.

Choose Save changes after editing. Phones pick up the change at their next daily check. To push it to a phone now, use Reprovision on that phone's page.

The list of profiles shows a Ready badge, or the first problem, for example:

  • No model template inherits from this family yet. The family has no templates for any model, so no phone can use it.
  • Template … is missing; devices cannot be provisioned. The template was deleted or failed to load. Pick another template.

Delete a profile

Delete works only while no phone uses the profile. Move its phones to another profile first: filter the Devices list by the profile (view on the profile's page) and change each phone's Device profile.

If something doesn't work

  • A model is missing from "Models served". The template family has no template for that model. Check Supported phones and adapters.
  • "A device profile with that name exists in this organization." Choose another name.
  • "only one zone can be the default group" (or priority, or emergency). Give that role to a single zone.
  • A setting is refused (for example has an invalid format). The template only allows certain values. Read the setting's description on the template's Variables tab.

guides.title: Phone keys
guides.summary: Set up the programmable keys on desk phones (lines, busy lamps, speed dials, paging, parking and more) and decide which keys users may change.

headings.title: A different key list for one phone

guides.html:
Most desk phones have a row of buttons with a small light next to each one. Veyra sets these keys for you. You make the key list once in a device profile, and every phone of that profile gets the same keys in the same order.

Edit the key list

  1. Open the profile under Provisioning → Device Profiles. The Line keys heading holds the list.
  2. Choose Add key. A new key starts as a busy lamp (BLF).
  3. Pick the key type, fill in what it needs (below), and optionally a Label, the text shown next to the key. Without a label the phone shows the name of what the key calls.
  4. Use the up and down arrows to change the order, and the bin to remove a key.
  5. Choose Save changes.

The first key in the list is the phone's first programmable key. The phone's own line always comes first with a key of its own, so you do not need to add it; add more lines, BLF, speed dial, paging and other keys here. A profile can have up to 48 keys. A phone with fewer buttons uses the first ones (some phones show the rest on extra pages).

Key types

TypeWhat you enterWhat the key does
LineA line number, 1 to 8Shows one of the phone's lines (extensions).
BLF (watch a phone or group)An extension or ring group numberThe light shows when that number is busy or ringing. Press it to call, or to pick up a call ringing there.
Speed dialA numberCalls the number. You can type it with spaces, dashes or brackets, such as +1 (573) 555-0100; Veyra keeps only the digits, *, # and +.
Page a zoneA paging zonePages the zone. Choose From a variable (per building)… to use a provisioning variable such as $all_call instead, so each building pages its own zone.
User's choice (set from My Phone)NothingAn open slot the phone's user fills (see below).
VoicemailA line number, or nothing for line 1Calls voicemail. The light shows waiting messages.
Intercom to an extensionAn extension numberCalls the extension, which answers on its speaker by itself.
Do Not Disturb (lit while on)NothingTurns Do Not Disturb on and off for this phone.
Park (a lot, or watch a slot)A parking lot, such as front-desk, or a lot and slot, such as front-desk:2972With a lot: parks the current call. With a slot: lights while a call is parked there; press it to pick the call up.
Toggle (call flow, time condition, queue log-in)flow:<call flow>, tc:<time condition>, agent or queue:<queue>Switches a call flow or a time condition override, or logs the phone in and out of its queues (agent) or one queue. The light is on while it is switched or logged in.
TransferNothingTransfers the current call. Not every phone has a transfer key: where it has none, the preview says so and the phone's own soft key does it.
Presence of a colleagueAn extension numberLit while the colleague is busy or in a meeting, blinking while away, off when available. Press it to call them.

For the voicemail, intercom, presence, park and toggle types, a hint under the value field says what to enter. For speed dial, BLF, intercom and presence keys, spaces, dashes and brackets in the number are removed when you save.

Parking lots, call flows, time conditions and queues are referred to by their short name (slug), as shown on their own pages. Veyra checks each one when you save. A time condition needs an override code before a toggle key can switch it.

Any value can be a provisioning variable written as $name, for example $front_office. Each phone then takes the value defined for its site or profile. See Provisioning variables.

Keys that users choose themselves

Add keys of the type User's choice (set from My Phone) to leave open slots. The person whose extension is on the phone can then put a speed dial, a busy lamp or a presence key in each open slot from My Phone in Veyra.

Every other key is locked: users see it with a padlock and cannot change it. Use this for keys everyone must keep, such as an all-call paging key.

An administrator can change a user's keys too. On the phone's page, open the Line keys tab. When the profile has open slots and the phone has an extension, the User's keys card shows each key: Set or Change an open slot, or Clear it. The phone picks up the change within a minute.

A different key list for one phone

  1. Open the phone under Provisioning → Devices and go to the Line keys tab.
  2. Tick Override the profile's keys for this phone. The profile's keys are copied as a starting point.
  3. Change the list and choose Save changes.

From now on this phone ignores changes to the profile's keys. Untick the box and save to go back to the profile's keys.

If something doesn't work

Veyra checks every key when you save and names the key that is wrong:

  • key 3: enter a number to dial or watch. A BLF, speed dial, intercom or presence key needs a number: digits, *, # and + (spaces, dashes and brackets are removed).
  • a line key names a line number 1-8.
  • paging zone … not found, parking lot … not found, call flow … not found, queue … not found. Check the short name on that item's page.
  • the time condition … has no override code. Give the time condition an override code first.

If a key does not appear on the phone, open the phone's Configuration tab and choose Render. A key that uses a variable nobody defined is listed under Missing variables and is left out until you define it.

guides.title: Analog adapters and fax machines
guides.summary: Connect analog phones, door phones and fax machines through a Grandstream HT80x or HT81x adapter.

headings.title: What the adapter does for you

guides.html:
An analog telephone adapter (ATA) lets an ordinary analog phone or a fax machine use Veyra. Veyra configures Grandstream adapters:

  • HT801 (one phone port) and HT802 (two), also the V2 versions;
  • HT812 (two ports), HT814 (four) and HT818 (eight), also the V2 versions.

These templates are experimental: test one adapter before rolling out more (see Supported phones and adapters).

Set up an adapter

  1. Create one extension for each port you will use (under Telephony → Extensions).
  2. Create a device profile with the template Grandstream HT801 / HT802 or Grandstream HT812 / HT814 / HT818, or the family Grandstream ATA (common settings).
  3. Register the adapter under Provisioning → Devices with its MAC address and model (see Add a phone).
  4. On the device's Settings tab, set Extension (line 1) to port 1's extension. Add the other ports with Add line under Extra lines: line 2 is port 2, line 3 is port 3, and so on.
  5. Point the adapter at Veyra: in its web page, Maintenance → Upgrade and Provisioning, choose HTTPS, the server <your Veyra server>/provisioning, and the organization's enrollment user name and password. Or use DHCP option 66. See Connect phones to Veyra.

After it restarts, each port with an extension registers. Ports without an extension are turned off. Lines beyond the adapter's ports (line 3 on an HT802, for example) are ignored.

What the adapter does for you

  • Star codes go to Veyra. The adapter's own star codes are turned off, so *97 (voicemail), *72, *78 and the other Veyra codes work from the analog phone. To use the adapter's own codes instead, turn on the setting local_call_features in the profile.
  • Voicemail waiting: a stutter dial tone, and the light on phones that have one.
  • Hotline: a phone that dials one number as soon as it is picked up, for example a lobby or elevator phone. Set Hotline number (and, for a short pause first, Warm-line delay (seconds)) on the port's extension.

Fax machines

Plug the fax machine straight into a port of the adapter, with no splitter. Faxes can travel two ways:

  • As audio (G.711 pass-through). Works with any carrier. This is the default for every port.
  • As T.38. A fax protocol that copes much better with a poor network. It needs a carrier that supports T.38.

To use T.38 for a fax machine:

  1. Open the port's extension and turn on Fax machine (T.38). Deploy the change as the page asks.
  2. Turn on T.38 for the carrier on its SIP trunk (Fax over T.38).
  3. Use Reprovision on the adapter's device page. With the profile setting fax_mode on auto (the default), the adapter switches that port to T.38 by itself.

fax_mode can also force every port to passthrough (audio) or t38.

Keep error correction (ECM) on in the fax machine, and look at its result report after a test fax. A fax that fails as audio usually means packet loss or jitter on the network; T.38 end to end is the fix where the carrier supports it.

Other adapter settings

These are in the device profile under Settings:

SettingWhat it does
admin_passwordThe password of the adapter's web page. Blank keeps the one on the sticker.
polling_hourThe hour (0–23) the adapter checks Veyra for changes each day.
install_caInstalls the Veyra certificate on the adapter (on by default).
validate_server_certificateMakes the adapter refuse a server it does not trust. Turn it on once the certificate is installed.
dhcp_overrideLets DHCP options 43, 66 or 160 replace the server set by Veyra. Off keeps the adapter on Veyra over HTTPS.

If something doesn't work

  • The adapter does not get its configuration. See If something doesn't work in Connect phones to Veyra. Grandstream adapters do not use the plain-HTTP bootstrap, so point them at the https address.
  • A port gives no dial tone. Check that the port's line has an extension on the device's Settings tab, and that the extension is enabled.
  • Faxes fail. Try the port as audio first (turn Fax machine (T.38) off). If audio works and T.38 does not, the carrier may not support T.38.

guides.title: Customize a provisioning template
guides.summary: Change what Veyra writes into phones' configuration files with your own template, edited in the browser, previewed, exported and imported.

headings.title: When Veyra updates an official template

guides.html:
A template turns what Veyra knows about a phone (its extensions, keys, paging zones, time zone…) into the files the phone downloads. Most of the time the official templates are all you need, and the settings in a device profile cover the rest. Make your own template when you need a phone setting that no profile setting offers.

You never change an official template. You make a local template that inherits from it and replaces only the parts you change. Veyra updates can then improve the official template without overwriting your work.

Templates are written in Jinja2, a simple text template language. You need to know the phone vendor's configuration parameter names. Test every change on one phone first.

Look at a template

Open Provisioning → Templates and click a template. The list shows each template's models (or Base template for a family), version and source: Official, Community or Local, plus a status badge when it is not stable.

The template's page has these tabs:

  • Overview: manufacturer, models, the firmware it was written for, its features and description. Inheritance and files shows the chain of templates it inherits from and the files it produces (for example {mac}.cfg).
  • Variables: the settings a profile or device can give, with their type, default, and whether they are required or secret.
  • Preview: fill in sample values, pick a model and a MAC address, and choose Render preview to see the files. Secrets are masked. Base templates cannot be previewed: open one of their model templates.
  • Edit: only on local templates, for people who may change provisioning.

Make an editable copy

  1. Open the official template and choose Customize.
  2. Fill in:
    • Template key (required): a unique name of lower-case letters and digits in two to eight parts separated by dots or dashes, for example local.vvx.450.
    • Name (required), for example Poly VVX 450 (ours).
    • Organization: the organization it belongs to. A platform administrator can leave it on Platform-wide (all organizations).
  3. Choose Create editable copy.

The copy starts at version 0.1.0, marked experimental, with nothing changed: each file just extends the official one and has an empty model_settings block where your changes go.

If you customize a family (base template), Veyra also makes a local model template under your copy for each model of the family. Point a profile at your family copy to use them.

When a phone's profile points at a family, Veyra uses a local model template in that family before the official one.
