So customizing a model template, such as Poly VVX 450, changes the files of every VVX 450 whose profile uses the Poly VVX family as soon as you save — in the template's organization only, or in every organization for a Platform-wide template. Other organizations neither use nor see an organization's local templates. Profiles that point at the official model template directly keep it.

Edit a local template

Open the local template and go to the Edit tab.

Template card

  • Name and Version (required). The version is a number like 0.1.1. Raise it when you change the template; the previous version is replaced, not kept.
  • Models: the model names this template serves, separated by commas. A family has no models of its own.
  • Status: Experimental, Stable (verified on hardware) or Deprecated.
  • Description.

Variables card

Variables are settings that a profile or device can fill in, used in a file as {{ name }}. Choose Add a variable and give it:

  • Name (required): lower-case letters, digits and _.
  • Type: Text, Number or Yes / no, and a Default.
  • Description: shown next to the field on the profile and device.
  • Required, and Secret (masked in previews, never exported, no default).
  • For text: an Allowed pattern (a regular expression the value must match) and a Maximum length.

Under Inherited from the parent you can give a different default to any setting the template inherits. Leave it empty to keep the parent's.

Files card

Pick a file under File and edit it in the box. In a template with a parent, the file starts with {% extends %}, and each {% block %} replaces that part of the parent's file.

The Insert a Veyra variable panel next to the box lists everything you can use. Click an entry to insert it where the cursor is. Search it, or open a section:

  • This template's values: its variables.
  • Device, Organization, Lines, Keys, Paging, Paging zones, Server, Features: what Veyra knows about the phone. Lines, keys and paging zones are lists: first insert the loop at the top of the section, then the entries inside it.
  • Provisioning variables: the provisioning variables defined under Provisioning → Variables, inserted as {{ vars.name }}. Each phone gets the value of its site, its organization or the installation.
  • Snippets: common patterns, such as Only when set, Yes/no as 1/0 and Override a block.

Choose Save template. Veyra checks the template first. If something is wrong, The template did not validate lists the problems and nothing is saved. Phones using the template get the change at their next check.

Export and import

  • Export (on any template) shows the template as JSON. Choose Copy JSON to save or share it. Exports never contain SIP passwords or other secrets.
  • Import template (on the Templates list) takes such JSON. Paste it under Template export (JSON), choose the Organization, then Validate. When it says Template is valid, choose Import. It becomes a local template.

Delete a local template

Delete works only when no device profile uses the template and no other template inherits from it.

When Veyra updates an official template

After a Veyra update, a local template whose official parent has a new version shows Parent updated in the list. Your template keeps working. Compare it with the new parent (open the parent from Inheritance and files) to see whether the parent now does what you added, or changed something you rely on.

If something doesn't work

  • "Template key … is already used." Choose another key.
  • The preview says "Could not render". The list names the problem, often a misspelled name or an unclosed {% if %} or {% for %}.
  • A setting you wrote does not reach the phone. Check that your change is inside a block that the parent file has. Text outside the blocks of a file with {% extends %} is ignored.
  • The Templates list shows "Some templates could not be loaded". A stored template failed its checks, for example after its parent changed, and it cannot be used or opened. The message names the template and the problem.

guides.title: Provisioning variables
guides.summary: Define a value once, such as each building's all-call paging zone or a time server, and let every phone take the value for its site or profile.

headings.title: Where a phone gets the value

guides.html:
A provisioning variable is a named value that phones share. You define it once, and phones use it in their keys and templates. The same name can have a different value per building. That way one device profile can serve every building: each phone's all-call key pages its own building's zone.

Where a phone gets the value

A variable can be defined for four scopes:

ScopeReaches
InstallationEvery phone on this Veyra server. Only platform administrators can define it.
OrganizationThe organization's phones.
SitePhones at that site (the phone's own site, or else its profile's site).
ProfilePhones using that device profile.

When the same name is defined at several scopes, each phone takes the nearest one: profile first, then site, then organization, then installation. Define a value at the widest scope that shares it, and override it only where it differs.

Define a variable

  1. Open Provisioning → Variables and choose New variable.
  2. Fill in:
    • Name (required): starts with a letter; lower-case letters, digits and underscores, up to 40 characters. For example all_call. Some names are reserved because templates already use them (for example timezone), and Veyra says so.
    • Defined for: the scope. For Site or Profile, also choose which one. With more than one organization, choose the Organization.
    • Value: up to 1000 characters.
    • Description: what the value is for.
    • Sensitive (shown masked to those who cannot change it): for passwords.
  3. Choose Create variable.

A name can be defined only once per scope: one all_call for the organization, one for each site, and so on.

To change a value, click the variable in the list, change it and choose Save. A sensitive value is not shown again; leave the field empty to keep it, or type a new one.

When you create, change or remove a variable, Veyra asks every phone it reaches to read its configuration again, and tells you how many phones it asked. Phones that are not registered right now get the change at their next daily check.

Use a variable

  • In a key or zone: type $name as the value. For a paging key, choose From a variable (per building)… and type the name. See Phone keys.
  • In a template: write {{ vars.name }}. See Customize a provisioning template.

The Use column of the list shows both forms for each variable.

Example: one all-call key for every building

  1. Create a paging zone for each building's all-call (under Telephony → Paging Zones).
  2. Define all_call for site Building A with the value building-a-all-call (the zone's short name), and for site Building B with its zone's short name.
  3. In the profile, add a key of type Page a zone, choose From a variable (per building)… and type $all_call.

Each phone now pages its own building.

Built-in values

The Built-in values card lists the values every template has without any definition: they come from the phone, its extension and the server (for example the SIP user name, the server address and the time zone). You cannot define variables with these names.

See what a phone gets

Open the phone under Provisioning → Devices, go to the Configuration tab, and look at the Variables card. It lists every variable that reaches the phone, its value, and the scope it came from. Render shows the files; a variable that a key or template uses but nobody defined is listed under Missing variables, and the setting or key is left out.

Remove a variable

Click the variable, choose Remove, then Yes, remove. Phones that use the name then take it from a wider scope if there is one.

Veyra refuses to remove it (Variable in use) if some phone's keys use $name and no other scope would give that phone a value. The message names those phones. Change their keys, or define the value at another scope first.

If something doesn't work

  • "… is already defined at this scope." Click the existing variable in the list and change it instead.
  • A phone does not show the new value. Check its Variables card: a nearer scope (its profile, for example) may define the same name. If the value is right there, choose Reprovision on the phone's page.
  • The site you need is not in the list. Sites are created under Directory → Sites.

guides.title: Phone firmware
guides.summary: Upload the vendor's firmware for your phones and let Veyra update them, per profile or per phone.
guides.html:
Phones run software from their maker, called firmware. Veyra can keep your phones on the version you choose: you upload the vendor's firmware file once and assign it to a device profile. Each phone compares the version at its next check, updates itself and restarts.

If you assign nothing, Veyra leaves the phones' firmware alone.

Upload a firmware image

  1. Download the firmware file from the vendor's support site. For Poly VVX phones, that is the sip.ld file of the UC Software release. For Grandstream, keep the vendor's file name (for example grp26xxafw.bin or gxp2170fw.bin), because the phone asks for its file by name.
  2. Open Provisioning → Firmware and choose Upload firmware.
  3. Fill in:
    • File: the firmware file, up to 512 MB. Its name may contain only letters, digits, ., _ and -. Do not rename it.
    • Manufacturer (required): pick it from the list, which shows the manufacturers Veyra has templates for. Profiles only offer images whose manufacturer matches their template's.
    • Version (required): the version number, for example 6.4.5.1234. Type it exactly as the phone reports it, so Veyra can tell whether the phone is up to date.
    • Models: the models it is for, separated by commas, for example VVX 411, VVX 450. Leave it empty when the file fits every model of the manufacturer.
    • Notes: for your own records.
  4. Choose Upload.

The list shows each image with its file name, models, size, the start of its SHA-256 checksum (to compare with the vendor's), who uploaded it, and how many profiles and phones it is assigned to.

Edit on a row changes the image's Models and Notes. To change the file, manufacturer or version, upload it again and delete the old image.

Roll it out

  1. Test on one phone first: open the phone under Provisioning → Devices and choose the image under Firmware override on the Settings tab. Save, then choose Reprovision.
  2. When it works, open the device profile under Provisioning → Device Profiles, choose the image under Firmware and save. Every phone of the profile updates at its next daily check. To update one now, use Reprovision on its page.
  3. Remove the test phone's override again (set Firmware override back to From the profile).
A phone restarts to install firmware, which takes several minutes. It cannot make calls in the meantime. Roll out to a profile at a quiet time, or leave it to the phones' daily check, which runs at night by default.

Poly phones also go down to an older version if you assign one, so you can undo an update the same way.

Check progress

On each phone's page, the Status tab shows under Firmware:

  • Assigned: the version Veyra wants, and whether it comes from the profile or the phone.
  • Running: the version the phone reported at its last check.
  • State: Up to date, Update pending, or Unknown until the phone has checked in.

Delete an image

The bin on a row works only when no profile or phone uses the image. Phones that already run the version are not affected.

If something doesn't work

  • The image is not offered in a profile or on a phone. Its Manufacturer does not match the template's manufacturer. Upload it again with the right manufacturer, then delete the old one.
  • "… is already uploaded." The same manufacturer, version and file name exist already.
  • "Update pending" stays. The phone has not checked in since, or the version you typed differs from what the phone reports. Compare Running with Assigned; if the phone runs the right firmware but the text differs, upload the image again with the version as the phone shows it.
  • The phone does not update. Check that the file is the right one for the model. Some phones refuse firmware for another model, or a jump over several major versions; the vendor's release notes say which steps are needed.

guides.title: Set the My Phone layout for groups of users
guides.summary: Choose which widgets people see on My Phone by organization, building, department or role, and lock the ones they must keep.
guides.html:
My Phone is each user's own page: their phone's settings, voicemail, calls, contacts and more, arranged as widgets on one or more tabs. Users can rearrange it themselves (see Your phone at a glance: My Phone). A portal layout is the arrangement they start with. You can make different layouts for different groups, for example a simple one for classrooms and a fuller one for the front office, and you can lock widgets so users cannot remove them.

Layouts are managed under System → Portal Layouts. You need the portal.templates permission.

Which layout a user gets

Each layout Applies to one scope:

  • A role: users who have that role,
  • A department: users whose extension is in that department,
  • A building: users whose extension is in that building,
  • Whole organization,
  • System-wide (every organization): platform administrators only.

A user gets the nearest one, in that order: a role's layout wins over a department's, which wins over a building's, then the organization's, then the system-wide one. When two layouts of the same scope match, the higher Priority (0 to 100) wins. Departments and buildings are taken from the user's first extension. Users with no matching layout see the built-in arrangement.

Create a layout

  1. Choose New layout.
  2. Enter a Name and, if you like, a Description.
  3. Choose Applies to, the Organization, and the Building, Department or Role when the scope needs one. These cannot be changed later.
  4. Arrange the widgets:
    • The layout starts from the built-in arrangement. Add a widget with its button above the canvas (My phone, Presence, Voicemail, Recent calls, Contacts, Colleagues, Phone keys, Fax, Conference, Codes you can dial, Announcement).
    • Drag a widget by its title bar, resize it from the corner, and remove it with its ×.
    • Add a tab with Tab (up to 8), rename the current tab in the box beside it, and remove it with the bin icon.
  5. For each widget users must keep, turn on Users cannot remove it.
  6. Leave Enabled on and choose Save.

The Announcement widget

Announcement shows a note from you to everyone with this layout, for example Fire drill Thursday 10:00. Type it in the widget's Text box. Users cannot add this widget themselves; lock it so they cannot remove it either.

What users can change

Users choose Arrange on My Phone to move, resize, add and remove widgets and tabs. Their arrangement is saved for them and stays theirs: later changes to the layout do not overwrite it. Locked widgets are the exception: a user cannot remove them, and if a locked widget is missing from their page, it is put back on their first tab.

To give everyone the current version of a layout, open it and choose Push to users. Every user who gets this layout loses their own arrangement and sees the layout again on their next visit. Their other settings stay.

Delete a layout

Open it and choose Delete. Users fall back to the next matching layout or the built-in one; their own arrangements stay.

Good to know

  • A widget that shows one extension or voicemail box (My phone, Presence, Voicemail) shows the user's first one. Users with several can add more and pick which.
  • A user with no extension and no voicemail box sees No phone is assigned to you on My Phone instead of the widgets.

guides.title: See which phones are registered
guides.summary: Check which phones are connected to Veyra right now, where they connect from, and whether the carriers' trunks are registered.
guides.html:
A phone is registered when it has signed in to Veyra with its extension's SIP user name and password. Only a registered phone rings and can make calls. Telephony → Registrations lists every phone registered right now. The page refreshes itself every 10 seconds; Refresh updates it at once.

The phones table

ColumnWhat it shows
ExtensionThe extension number and name. If the extension allows only a set number of phones, also how many of them are registered, for example 1 of 2 phones registered.
Registers fromThe network address the registration arrived from. Behind NAT means the phone is behind a router that changes its address, for example a phone at home.
Phone's own addressThe address the phone says it has, and the transport (UDP, TCP or TLS). It differs from Registers from when the phone is behind NAT.
Phone reportsWhat the phone says it is: usually the brand, model and firmware version.
ReachabilityReachable with the round-trip time in milliseconds, Unreachable when the phone stopped answering Veyra's checks, or Not checked.
ExpiresWhen the registration runs out. The phone renews it well before then.

Search by extension, address or phone model. With more than one organization, you can show one at a time.

The blue box … enabled extensions have no registered phone counts the extensions nobody is signed in to. They are marked Not registered on the Extensions page.

The trunks table

If the server has SIP trunks to carriers, the Trunks card shows Veyra's own registration to each one:

  • Registration: Registered, Reachable, Registering, Not registered, Registration rejected, Unreachable or Unknown.
  • Engine says: the raw status from the telephony engine.
  • Host: whether the carrier's server answers (Answers or No answer).

If something doesn't work

  • A phone is missing from the list.
    1. Open the phone under Provisioning → Devices. If its status is Never provisioned or Error, it never got its configuration: see Connect phones to Veyra.
    2. Check that the phone has an Extension (line 1) and that the extension is enabled.
    3. If more phones use the extension than it allows, the phone that registers last replaces the earliest one, so two phones on one extension keep pushing each other out.
  • Unreachable. The phone registered but no longer answers. It may have been unplugged, or a router between them is dropping traffic. Phones behind NAT are the usual case; check the router at that location.
  • "Registration details are not available". The telephony engine is not running or cannot report addresses. The message says why. Look at the system health pages.
  • A trunk shows "Registration rejected". The carrier refused the user name or password. Check the trunk's settings with the carrier.

guides.title: Connect a SIP trunk
guides.summary: Connect Veyra to your phone carrier so calls can reach and leave the building.
guides.html:
A SIP trunk is the connection between Veyra and your phone carrier (for example a SIP provider or your phone company's SIP service). Incoming calls arrive on a trunk, and outgoing calls leave through one. Veyra can have several trunks, for example a main carrier and a backup.

A trunk on its own does nothing with calls. After you add it:

  • Route incoming calls tells Veyra where each of your phone numbers rings.
  • Route outgoing calls tells Veyra which dialled numbers go out through which trunk.

Trunks are set up at Telephony → SIP Trunks.

Before you start

  • Only platform administrators can add or change trunks. Organization administrators can see the list so they can pick a trunk on an inbound route.
  • Ask the carrier which of the two ways of connecting they use, and for the details below.
Ask the carrier forUsed for
The SIP server's host name or IP address, and the port (usually 5060)Host and Port
UDP, TCP or TLSTransport
Whether they use registration or IP authenticationAuthentication
For registration: the user name and passwordUser name, Password
For IP authentication: the addresses their calls come fromMatch addresses
Which of your numbers you may send as caller IDDefault caller ID
How many calls at once your plan allowsMaximum channels
Whether they support T.38 faxFax over T.38

With IP authentication, the carrier also needs to know your public IP address, so they accept calls from it.

Registration or IP authentication

  • Registration: Veyra signs in to the carrier with a user name and password, much like a desk phone signs in to Veyra. Common with smaller SIP providers. Both the user name and password are required.
  • IP authentication: the carrier trusts calls coming from your server's address, and there is no sign-in. Veyra recognises incoming calls from the carrier by the address they come from. Common with larger carriers and dedicated circuits.

1. Create the trunk

  1. Choose New trunk.
  2. Fill in the essentials:
    • Name: anything that helps you recognise it, such as Carrier A.
    • Authentication: Registration or IP authentication.
    • Host, Port and Transport.
    • For registration: User name and Password.
    • For IP authentication: Match addresses, one address or network (such as 198.51.100.0/24) per line. Leave it empty if calls come from the Host itself.
    • Default caller ID: the number sent on outgoing calls when neither the route nor the extension sets one. Digits only, with an optional leading +.
  3. Choose Create trunk. Veyra opens the trunk's page.

The password is stored encrypted and is never shown again. To change it later, type a new one in Set new password; leave it empty to keep the stored one.

2. Check the other settings

The trunk's page shows every setting, in sections. Most can stay as they are.

Connection

  • Enabled: a disabled trunk is kept but left out of the phone system. Routes that use it skip it and try their next trunk.

Authentication

  • Authentication user name: only when the carrier gives you a sign-in name that differs from the user name.
  • In IP mode a password is optional, for carriers that still ask for one on outgoing calls. Clear the stored password removes it.

Identification

  • Match addresses: in registration mode these are optional extra addresses whose calls are accepted as this trunk.

Calling

  • Codecs: keep Installation default (the list under System → Telephony Engine) unless the carrier asks for something specific. Untick it to choose codecs for this trunk only.
  • Maximum channels: how many calls at once the carrier allows. Empty means unlimited. When it is full, Veyra skips this trunk and tries the route's next one.
  • Channels kept for emergency calls: of the maximum, how many ordinary calls may not use, so a 911 call can always get out. The default is 1. It only works when Maximum channels is set. Emergency calls are never counted against the limit.
  • Caller ID header: how your number is passed to the carrier: P-Asserted-Identity (the default), Remote-Party-ID, or None (From header only). Change it only if the carrier asks.
  • DTMF: how key presses (for menus and voicemail PINs) are sent. Keep RFC 4733 (RTP events) unless the carrier says otherwise.
  • Fax over T.38: offers T.38 fax to this carrier. If the carrier declines, fax is sent as ordinary audio. Turn it on only if the carrier supports T.38.
  • Qualify frequency (seconds): how often Veyra checks that the carrier answers. 0 turns the check off, and the status then shows Unknown.
  • Registration timers (registration mode only): Registration expiry (seconds) (60–86400), Retry after a failure (seconds) (10–3600), Retry after Forbidden (seconds) (30–86400, used when the carrier refuses the sign-in) and Give up after (attempts) (empty means keep trying).

Advanced

  • From user, From domain and Outbound proxy are usually left empty. Fill them in only when the carrier's instructions ask for them.

Choose Save changes when you are done.

3. Deploy

Saving a trunk changes the phone system's configuration. A Changes not yet deployed note appears on the page, and Deploy changes appears in the top bar. Choose it to apply the change. Calls in progress are not interrupted.

You can deploy once, after you have also created your inbound and outbound routes.

4. Check the status

The Status column (and the badge at the top of the trunk's page) refreshes every 15 seconds:

StatusMeaning
OnlineThe carrier answers, and a registration trunk is registered
RegisteringVeyra is signing in to the carrier
Registration rejectedThe carrier refused the sign-in: check the user name, password and host
Not registeredThe registration has stopped
OfflineThe carrier does not answer Veyra's checks
UnknownThe trunk has not been deployed yet, the check is off, or the phone system does not report status right now
DisabledThe trunk is turned off

On the trunk's page, the Information card also shows Registration: with the word the phone system reports for the registration (for example Registered or Rejected). Quote it when you ask the carrier for help.

A registration trunk with no stored password shows a No password warning.

If it does not work

  • Registration rejected: re-enter the password in Set new password, check User name and Authentication user name, save and deploy.
  • Offline: check the Host, Port and Transport, and that your firewall allows SIP to and from the carrier.
  • Incoming calls are not answered on an IP trunk: the call may come from an address that is not in Match addresses. Ask the carrier for all the addresses they send calls from.
  • Calls connect but there is no audio, or audio in one direction only: this is usually a firewall or NAT problem, not a trunk setting.
  • Menu choices or PINs are not recognised: try another DTMF setting.

Deleting a trunk

Delete asks you to type the trunk's name. A trunk used by any inbound or outbound route cannot be deleted; Veyra lists the routes to change first. Deploy afterwards to remove it from the phone system.

guides.title: Set up a ring group
guides.summary: Give a team one number that rings several phones at once or in turn, and decide where unanswered calls go.

headings.title: 3. Decide what happens when nobody answers
Turn a group off or delete it

guides.html:
A ring group is a number that rings several phones. The front office, the help desk or the maintenance team get one number. When it is called, their phones ring all at once or one after the other. If nobody answers, the call goes on to a voicemail box, a menu or another number.

Use a ring group when a few people share the calls and someone usually answers within a few rings. When callers may have to wait for someone to become free, use a call queue instead: see Set up a call queue.

Before you start

  • You need permission to change ring groups and queues. Organization and site administrators have it by default.
  • The people in the group need extensions. A ring group rings extensions, plus up to 10 outside numbers such as mobiles.

1. Create the group

  1. Open Telephony → Ring Groups and choose New ring group.
  2. If you manage several organizations, choose the Organization.
  3. Enter a Name, for example Front office, and a Number. The number comes from the same numbering plan as extensions and queues, so it must not already be in use. The field suggests the next free number.
  4. Choose Create group. Veyra opens the group's page.

2. Choose who rings and how

On the group's page:

  • Members: choose an extension under Choose an extension to add and click Add. Repeat for each person. A group has at most 32 members. Use the arrows to change the order.
  • Outside numbers: mobile or other outside numbers, one per line, up to 10. They ring along with the members and are dialled through the organization's outbound routes. Tick Outside numbers must press 1 to accept so that a mobile's voicemail cannot answer the call and keep it.
  • Strategy: how the members ring.
StrategyWhat happens
Ring all members at onceEvery member rings for the ring time. The first to answer gets the call.
Ring members one after the otherThe first member in the list rings, then the second, and so on.
One at a time, starting after the last who answeredShares the calls out, starting with the member after whoever answered last.
One at a time, each call starting one member laterEach new call starts one place further down the list.
One at a time, longest without a call firstThe member who has gone longest without a call rings first.
  • Ring time (seconds): 5 to 120. With Ring all it is the time for the whole group. With the one-at-a-time strategies it is the time per member. Open Ring time per member to give one person a longer or shorter time.
  • Skip a member after unanswered calls (one-at-a-time strategies only): a member who lets this many calls in a row go unanswered (1 to 10) is passed over for Skip for (minutes). Answering a call clears it. Leave it empty to never skip anyone.
  • Ring members who are already on a call: off, a member on a call is skipped. On, their phone gets a second call (call waiting).
  • Caller ID prefix: a short text shown before the caller's name on the ringing phones, for example Front: , so people know which group the call came in on. Letters, digits, spaces and . ' & ( ) - : only, at most 40 characters.
  • Callers hear: Ringing tone, or Music on hold with a Hold music set (see Manage audio and hold music).

3. Decide what happens when nobody answers

Under When nobody answers, choose a destination: an extension, an extension's voicemail, a shared voicemail inbox, an IVR menu, another ring group, a call queue, an announcement, a conference room, a call flow, fax to email, the dial-by-name directory, or Hang up.

A group with no members sends every caller straight to this destination.

4. Save and deploy

  1. Choose Save changes.
  2. A blue Changes not yet deployed note appears. Choose Deploy changes in the top bar to send the change to the phone system. (If you do not have that button, a platform administrator deploys.)
  3. Point an inbound route or an IVR menu key at the group, or simply dial its number from any phone.

The As deployed card on the right sums up what the group will do once deployed.

Turn a group off or delete it

  • Switch off Enabled to leave the group out of the phone system without deleting it. Routes and menus that point at it are flagged.
  • Delete removes the group. Routes, menus, groups and queues that still point at it must be changed first; Veyra tells you which. The number stops working at the next deployment.

When it does not work

  • A problems badge, or the note This group will not work as configured: read the list. Common causes are no members, a disabled member extension, or a failover destination that was deleted.
  • A member's phone never rings: check the extension is enabled and its phone is registered. With Ring members who are already on a call off, a busy member is skipped. With a skip setting, the member may be passed over after missed calls.
  • An outside number never rings: the organization needs an outbound route that allows the number.
  • Nothing changed after saving: deploy the changes.
  • Answering for a colleague: a ringing member phone can be picked up with ** and its extension, or with *8 from a phone in the same pickup group. See Pick up a colleague's ringing phone.

guides.title: Route incoming calls
guides.summary: Decide where each of your phone numbers (DIDs) rings, with a different destination outside business hours.
guides.html:
Each phone number your carrier delivers to Veyra is called a DID (direct inward dialing number). An inbound route says where calls to one DID go: a person's phone, a voicemail box, a menu, a ring group and so on. Calls to a number without a route are refused.

Inbound routes are at Telephony → Inbound Routes. You need a working trunk first: see Connect a SIP trunk.

Before you start

  • Get the list of your numbers from the carrier, and ask in what form they send them: ten digits (5735550100), eleven (15735550100) or with a plus (+15735550100).
  • Create what the calls should reach first (the extension, ring group, menu and so on).
  • If calls should go elsewhere after hours, create the time condition first.

Create a route

  1. Choose New inbound route.
  2. If you manage several organizations, choose the Organization that owns the number.
  3. Fill in the route:
    • DID: the number, digits with an optional leading + (2 to 20 digits). Spaces, dashes, dots and brackets are removed for you. Enter any for a catch-all route that takes calls to every number without a route of its own.
    • Trunk: leave Any trunk unless the number should only be answered when it arrives on one particular trunk.
    • Destination: first the kind, then which one. See the table below.
    • Time condition: leave Always (no time condition), or pick one. With a time condition, an After-hours destination appears, and it is required.
    • Caller ID prefix: optional text put in front of the caller's name on the ringing phone, such as Sales:, so people can see which number was called. Up to 40 letters, digits, spaces and . ' & ( ) - :.
    • Description and Enabled.
  4. Choose Create route, then Deploy changes in the top bar.

Destinations

KindCalls go to
ExtensionOne phone (and its forwarding and voicemail as set on the extension)
Voicemail of an extensionStraight to that extension's voicemail; only extensions with a voicemail box are listed
Shared voicemail inboxA shared box, such as a department's
IVR menuA "press 1 for…" menu
Ring groupSeveral phones at once or in turn
Call queueA queue with hold music and agents
AnnouncementA recorded message
Conference roomA conference room
Call flowA day/night switch: see Day/night switches
Fax to emailA fax inbox
Custom dialplanA custom context (platform administrators only; see Deploy changes)
Dial-by-name directoryCallers spell a name on the keypad

How numbers are matched

  • North American numbers in any form. A ten-digit DID also answers calls the carrier sends as 1 + ten digits or +1 + ten digits, and the other way round. You cannot create two routes for the same number in different forms with the same trunk setting. The route's page shows the forms under Matches. Numbers of other lengths must match exactly.
  • One route per number per trunk setting. You can have one route for a number on Any trunk and another for the same number on a specific trunk. On that trunk, the trunk's own route wins.
  • The catch-all. An any route only takes calls whose number has no route of its own.

Business hours

With a Time condition, calls during the open hours go to the Destination, and calls at any other time, and on holidays, go to the After-hours destination. The list shows each route's destination by name, with its kind (such as IVR menu or Ring group) underneath, and the time condition and closed-hours destination.

To open or close early for a day (a snow day, an assembly), use the time condition's Force open or Force closed instead of editing the route. See Business hours and holidays.

Editing and deleting

Open a route from the list to change it, then Save changes and deploy. The Information panel shows the forms of the number that match, the destination and the after-hours destination.

Delete removes the route. After the next deployment, calls to that number are no longer answered.

If it does not work

  • The route shows "No destination" in red. What it pointed to was deleted or disabled. Calls to the number are refused until you choose a new destination.
  • Calls to a number are refused, but the route exists. Check that the route is Enabled and deployed, that the carrier sends the number in a form the route matches (see the call details in Call History), and that a Trunk restriction is not excluding the trunk the call arrives on.
  • Calls go to the after-hours destination during the day. Check the time condition's time zone and hours, and whether someone left it Forced closed.
  • A caller is rejected straight away. They may be on the organization's block list: see Block callers.
Organization administrators can create and change inbound routes for their own organization. The Trunk field can only be changed by people allowed to see the trunks.

guides.title: Set up a call queue
guides.summary: Let callers wait in line with music and announcements until an agent is free, and let agents log in and out.

headings.title: 3. Choose how calls are handed out
4. Decide what callers hear and how long they wait
See how the queue is doing

guides.html:
A call queue holds callers in line until someone is free to answer. Callers hear music and, if you like, announcements and their place in line. The people who answer are called agents. Use a queue for a help desk, an attendance line or any number where more calls arrive than people can take at once.

For a small team that answers within a few rings, a ring group is simpler: see Set up a ring group.

Before you start

  • You need permission to change ring groups and queues. Organization and site administrators have it by default.
  • Every agent needs an extension.
  • If callers should hear a greeting or a "please hold" message, add the recordings to the audio library first: see Manage audio and hold music.

1. Create the queue

  1. Open Telephony → Call Queues and choose New queue.
  2. If you manage several organizations, choose the Organization.
  3. Enter a Name, for example Help desk, and a Number from the numbering plan. The field suggests the next free number.
  4. Choose Create queue. Veyra opens the queue's page.

2. Add the agents

Under Agents, choose an extension and click Add. A queue has at most 64 agents. For each agent:

  • Penalty (the number box, 0 to 9): agents with a higher penalty ring only when every agent with a lower one is busy or absent. Leave everyone at 0 to treat them equally, or give back-up staff a 1.
  • Logs in: when ticked, the agent is a dynamic agent and takes queue calls only while logged in. When not ticked, the agent is always in the queue.

3. Choose how calls are handed out

  • Strategy:
StrategyWho rings
Ring all available agentsEvery free agent at once.
Round robin (continues where it left off)The next agent in turn.
Agent idle the longestThe agent who has gone longest without a queue call.
Agent with the fewest completed callsSpreads the calls evenly.
Random agentAny free agent.
Agents in the listed orderAlways the first free agent in the list. Use the arrows to set the order.
  • Agent ring time (seconds): 5 to 60, how long each attempt rings an agent.
  • Pause between attempts (seconds): 1 to 30.
  • Agent rest after a call (seconds): 0 to 600, time after a call before the agent gets the next one (for notes).

4. Decide what callers hear and how long they wait

  • Callers hear: Music on hold (with a Hold music set, or the built-in music), or Ringing tone.
  • Announcement on joining: played once before the caller starts waiting.
  • Announcement while waiting and Repeat every (seconds) (15 to 600): for example "All our staff are busy; your call is important to us".
  • Announce the caller's position in line, every 15 to 600 seconds.
  • Maximum wait (seconds): 0 for no limit, otherwise 30 to 3600. After that the caller goes to the destination below.
  • Maximum callers waiting: 0 for no limit, up to 100. A caller beyond the limit goes straight to the destination below.
  • Let callers wait when no agent is available: off, a caller goes straight to the destination below when no agent is logged in or free.
  • Break-out menu: an IVR menu whose keys callers may press while they wait, for example 1 to leave a voicemail. Tell callers about it in the announcement while waiting. The menu must be enabled. See Build a phone menu.
  • When the caller is not connected: where the call goes after the maximum wait, when the queue is full, or when nobody can take it. The same destinations as everywhere else, or Hang up.

5. Save and deploy

  1. Choose Save changes.
  2. Choose Deploy changes in the top bar when the Changes not yet deployed note appears.
  3. Point an inbound route or a menu key at the queue, or dial its number.

The As deployed card sums up what the queue does once deployed.

Agents logging in and out

Dynamic agents (those with Logs in ticked) are only in the queue while logged in. Changing their state takes effect at once and needs no deployment.

From the phone (default codes; your organization may have changed them under Feature Codes):

DialWhat it does
*45Log in or out of every queue this phone may join
*45 and the queue numberLog in or out of that queue only
*46Pause or resume in the queues (stay logged in, take no calls for a while)
*46 and the queue numberPause or resume in that queue only
*47 and the queue numberHear how many callers are waiting

From the web: the Agents card on the queue's page lists the dynamic agents as Logged in, Paused or Logged out. Next to the state it shows when it last changed and who changed it: a person's name for a change made on the web, or phone when the agent used a code. Use Log in / Log out and Pause / Resume to change an agent, for example when someone forgot to log out before going home. Every change is written to the audit log.

Agents who are always in the queue (Logs in not ticked) cannot be logged out or paused.

See how the queue is doing

Reports shows, for each queue, the callers, how many were answered, how many hung up while waiting, the average wait and the share answered within 20 seconds. See Call history and reports.

When it does not work

  • Callers go straight to the failover: no agent is logged in or free, and Let callers wait when no agent is available is off. Or the queue has no agents.
  • An agent never gets calls: check that they are logged in and not paused (the Agents card), that their extension is enabled, and their penalty.
  • The phone says the code is not allowed: the extension's class of service may not allow that feature code.
  • Nothing changed after saving: deploy the changes. Only logging in, out and pausing apply without deploying.

guides.title: Pick up a colleague's ringing phone
guides.summary: Let people answer a call ringing on a nearby phone with *8 or ** and the extension, and set who may do it.
guides.html:
When a phone rings at an empty desk, a colleague can answer the call from their own phone. There are two ways:

DialWhat it answers
*8Any call ringing on a phone in the same pickup group
** and the extension, for example **2001The call ringing on that one phone

These two codes are fixed and cannot be changed under Feature Codes.

Who may pick up

  • *8 only works between phones in the same pickup group. A phone that is in no pickup group cannot use it.
  • ** and an extension works between any two phones of the organization, unless the organization is set to allow it only within pickup groups. That setting is on the organization's page under Directory → Organizations, Answer another phone's call: Any phone of the organization or Only phones in the same pickup group. A change there needs a deployment.

Create a pickup group

You need permission to change ring groups, queues and pickup groups. Organization and site administrators have it by default.

  1. Open Telephony → Pickup Groups and choose New pickup group.
  2. If you manage several organizations, choose the Organization.
  3. Enter a Name, for example Front office, and optionally a Description.
  4. Under Members, choose each extension and click Add. A group has at most 64 members. An extension can be in several pickup groups.
  5. Choose Create group.
  6. Choose Deploy changes in the top bar.

Group the phones that sit together and cover for each other: an office, a wing, a reception desk and its back office.

A group needs at least two members to be useful; the Status column warns when it has fewer.

Change or delete a group

  • Click a group, or its Edit button, to change its name or members, then Save changes and deploy.
  • The bin button deletes the group. Its members can no longer pick up each other's calls with *8 after the next deployment.

When it does not work

  • *8 does nothing: the two phones are not in the same pickup group, or the change has not been deployed. *8 only picks up a call that is ringing right now.
  • Directed pickup does nothing (** and the extension): the organization may allow it only within pickup groups (see above), or the phone belongs to another organization.
  • Ring groups: phones ringing because of a ring group can be picked up the same way. The group's own number cannot be picked up; pick up one of its ringing member phones.

guides.title: Route outgoing calls
guides.summary: Decide which dialled numbers go out to the carrier, through which trunks, and with which caller ID.

headings.title: Warnings at the top of the page

guides.html:
An outbound route says which numbers people may dial to the outside world and which trunk carries those calls. Without any outbound route, phones can only call other extensions.

Outbound routes are at Telephony → Outbound Routes. Only platform administrators can create or change them. You need at least one trunk first: see Connect a SIP trunk.

Create the emergency route first. See Emergency calling (911).

How Veyra picks a route

  • Routes are tried in the order of the list. The first route with a pattern that matches the dialled number carries the call.
  • Emergency routes always come first, and the other routes cannot be moved above them.
  • Within a route, the trunks are tried in order. If a trunk is unavailable, full (its Maximum channels reached) or rejects the call as congested, the next one is tried. If the far end is busy or does not answer, that is the result: Veyra does not try another trunk.
  • If every trunk fails, the caller hears "all circuits are busy".
  • Extensions always win over outbound patterns, so a pattern can never take over an internal number.

Use the arrows in the Order column to move a route up or down. Deploy afterwards.

The For column shows whose phones may use each route: an organization, a site (emergency routes), or both. Every organization (or Every phone with one organization) means the route is not limited.

Dial patterns

Each route has one or more patterns. A pattern has three parts:

PartWhat it does
Prefix (stripped)Digits the person dials first that are not sent to the carrier, such as an outside-line 9. Optional
MatchThe number itself, using pattern letters
PrependDigits added in front before the number is sent, such as 1 for long distance. Optional

Pattern letters in Match:

LetterMeans
Xany digit 0–9
Zany digit 1–9
Nany digit 2–9
[2-5]one digit from the range or list
.one or more of anything (only at the end)
!zero or more of anything (only at the end)

Examples for North America:

PrefixMatchPrependPeople dialSent to the carrier
NXXNXXXXXX57355501005735550100
1NXXNXXXXXX1573555010015735550100
9NXXNXXXXXX19573555010015735550100
NXXXXXX57355501005735550100 (seven-digit local dialling)
011.01144…01144… (international)

A route can have up to 50 patterns. Two patterns in one route may not be the same.

Create a route

  1. Choose New outbound route.
  2. Fill in:
    • Name, such as Local and long distance.
    • Caller ID number (optional): see below.
    • Used by (only shown when there are several organizations): All organizations, or one. A route of one organization is never used by the others' phones.
    • Emergency route: only for 911 and similar numbers.
    • For the phones of (emergency routes only): Every site, or one site. A route bound to a site is tried first for that site's phones and hands other phones to the next emergency route.
    • Dial patterns: at least one. Add pattern adds a row.
    • Trunks: choose a trunk and Add trunk. Add a second trunk as a backup if you have one, and order them with the arrows. At least one trunk is required.
    • Description and Enabled.
  3. Choose Create route. It is added at the end of its group (emergency or other).
  4. Move it into place with the arrows, then Deploy changes in the top bar.

Caller ID on outgoing calls

The number the called person sees is chosen in this order:

  1. On an emergency route: the extension's emergency caller ID, or else its site's (see Emergency calling (911)).
  2. The route's Caller ID number, if Always send this caller ID is ticked.
  3. The extension's own Outbound caller ID number (set on the extension's page).
  4. The route's Caller ID number.
  5. The trunk's Default caller ID.
  6. Otherwise, the caller's own number as is, which the carrier may reject or replace.

The Caller ID column shows From the extension when the route has no number of its own.

Most carriers only accept numbers that belong to you. Set the trunk's Default caller ID to your main number so there is always a valid one.

Warnings at the top of the page

Veyra checks the routes and lists problems under Check these routes:

  • No enabled emergency route: 911 dialled from a phone will not reach a carrier. Fix this first.
  • Extensions with no emergency caller ID: enabled extensions with no emergency caller ID of their own or on their site, while an emergency route has no caller ID number. The trunk's default number is sent for their emergency calls. See Emergency calling (911).
  • Route … has no enabled trunk: its calls will fail. A disabled trunk is shown struck through in the Trunks column.

Who may use which route

By default every phone may use every route. To limit what some phones can dial (for example classroom phones that may only make local calls), see Who can call where. Emergency routes always work, whatever the phone's class.

If it does not work

  • The caller hears "all circuits are busy". Every trunk on the route failed. Check the trunks' status on SIP Trunks, and their Maximum channels.
  • The call reaches the wrong route. An earlier route has a pattern that matches too. Move the more specific route higher.
  • The carrier rejects the call. Check the number format it expects (with or without 1, with +) and adjust Prepend, and check that the caller ID is one of your numbers.
  • Nothing happens when people dial. The number may not match any pattern, or the change was not deployed.

guides.title: Business hours and holidays
guides.summary: Set opening hours, holidays and closed days, so calls outside them go to a different destination.
guides.html:
A time condition is a schedule: the hours you are open, plus holidays and other closed days. On its own it does nothing. You pick it on an inbound route, and the route then sends calls during the open hours to its normal destination and calls at any other time to its after-hours destination.

Time conditions are at Telephony → Time Conditions. The list shows whether each one is Open now or Closed now, its hours, and how many routes use it.

Create a time condition

  1. Choose New time condition.
  2. If you manage several organizations, choose the Organization.
  3. Fill in:
    • Name, such as Office hours.
    • Time zone: leave it empty to use the organization's time zone, or enter a name such as America/Chicago.
    • Open hours: see below.
    • Holidays and closed days: see below.
    • Override code index and Override PIN (optional): see Open or close early.
  4. Choose Create time condition.
  5. Open an inbound route, pick the time condition, choose the After-hours destination, save, and choose Deploy changes in the top bar.

Open hours

Each range is a set of days and a time: click the day buttons (Mon to Sun) to turn days on or off, and set From and Until. A new time condition starts with Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 17:00.

  • Add range adds another, for example Saturday 09:00 to 12:00.
  • A call counts as open if it falls within any range. Until is not included: with 08:00 to 17:00, a call at 17:00 is after hours.
  • A range cannot cross midnight. For hours such as 22:00 to 06:00, add two ranges: 22:00 to 23:59, and 00:00 to 06:00 on the following days.
  • A time condition needs at least one range, and can have up to 50.

Holidays and closed days

On these days the condition is closed all day, whatever the open hours say.

  • Add holiday adds a date that repeats. Under Repeats, choose:
    • Same date every year, such as 25 December. Tick Several days in a row for a period such as 21 December to 2 January (it may cross New Year).
    • A weekday of a month, such as the Fourth Thursday of November (Thanksgiving) or the Last Monday of May (Memorial Day). The last weekday of February is not supported.
  • Add closed day adds a one-off date, such as a snow day, with an optional Until date for a period such as this year's winter break.

Each holiday shows a plain description below it so you can check it. A time condition can have up to 100.

One-off closed days stay in the list after they pass. Remove old ones from time to time.

Open or close early

On the time condition's page, the Override panel shows what the schedule says and what callers get right now.

  • Force open or Force closed changes what callers get immediately. No deployment is needed.
  • With Temporary: ends when the schedule next changes state ticked (the default), the override ends by itself at the next opening or closing time. Untick it to keep the override until someone chooses Back to the schedule.
  • The panel shows who forced it and when. The list shows a Forced badge.

People can also do this from a phone. Give the time condition an Override code index from 0 to 99, unique within the organization. Phones then dial the time-condition override feature code (*27 by default) followed by the index, for example *271, to force the opposite state until the schedule changes. Dialling it again clears it. A busy lamp field (BLF) key programmed with that code lights while the condition is forced. With an Override PIN (4 to 10 digits), the phone asks for the PIN first.

Editing and deleting

Change the schedule on the time condition's page, then Save changes and deploy. The Information panel lists the open hours and holidays as Veyra understands them.

A time condition used by an inbound route cannot be deleted. Remove it from those routes first.

If it does not work

  • Calls go after hours when you are open, or the reverse. Check the time zone shown under Information, and whether the condition is forced (Callers get says forced).
  • A schedule change has no effect. It needs Deploy changes. Only Force open and Force closed take effect without a deployment.
  • The phone code does nothing. Check the code on the time condition's page under Phone code, and that the feature code is turned on at Feature Codes.

For a switch that people flip by hand rather than a schedule (for example "night mode" when the office closes), see Day/night switches.

guides.title: Park calls
guides.summary: Set up a parking lot so a call can be put on hold at one phone and picked up from any other.
guides.html:
Parking puts a call on hold in a numbered slot that every phone can reach. The secretary answers a call for the principal, parks it, pages "call for Mrs Lee on 71", and Mrs Lee picks it up from the phone nearest to her.

How people use it

ToDo this
Park a callTransfer it to the lot's park extension (for example 70). The phone system reads back the slot number, for example 71.
Pick up a parked callDial the slot number (for example 71) from any phone. *85 and the slot number does the same.
See waiting callsA line key (BLF) set to a slot number lights while a call waits there.

If nobody picks the call up in time, the phone that parked it rings again. If that phone does not answer either, the call goes to the lot's destination.

Create a parking lot

You need permission to change ring groups, queues and conference rooms (organization and site administrators by default).

  1. Open Telephony → Parking and choose New parking lot.
  2. If you manage several organizations, choose the Organization.
  3. Enter a Name, the Park extension, the First slot and the Last slot. The suggested 70 with slots 71 to 79 suits most sites. Every one of these numbers must be free in the organization: not an extension, group or other number. The park extension must not lie inside the slot range, and a lot has at most 50 slots.
  4. Choose Create lot. Veyra opens the lot's page.

Set the timeout

On the lot's page:

  • Parked call times out after (seconds): 10 to 1800. Then the phone that parked the call rings.
  • Ring the parker for (seconds): 5 to 120.
  • When the parker does not answer: where the call goes then, for example the reception ring group or the main menu, or Hang up.
  • Play a courtesy tone when a call is picked up.
  • Enabled: a disabled lot is left out of the phone system.

Choose Save, then Deploy changes in the top bar. The On the phones card sums up what users do with the lot.

Line keys for slots

To give a receptionist a key per slot, add BLF keys with the slot numbers to the phone's line keys: on its device profile under Provisioning → Device Profiles, or for one phone in the Line keys card of the device's page. The key lights while a call waits in that slot, and pressing it picks the call up.

When it does not work

  • "Number in use" when creating the lot: one of the numbers is already used. Choose another range.
  • The transfer to the park extension fails: the lot is disabled or the change has not been deployed.
  • The parked call disappears: it timed out, rang the parker, then went to the lot's destination. Check the destination, or make the timeout longer.
  • Deleting a lot: its numbers become free again, and the lot leaves the phone system at the next deployment.

guides.title: Day/night switches (call flows)
guides.summary: Give staff a switch, on the web or on a phone key, that sends calls to a second destination until it is switched back.

headings.title: Send calls into the call flow

guides.html:
A call flow is a switch with two positions. Normally, calls that reach it go to one destination. While it is switched, they go to another. Staff flip it by hand: from Veyra, or from a desk phone with a code or a lit button.

Typical uses:

  • Night mode: the front office switches the main number to an after-hours message when the last person leaves.
  • Emergency closure: the main number plays a closure announcement on a snow day.
  • Cover: calls to a desk go to a colleague while someone is out.

For opening hours that follow a fixed schedule, use Business hours and holidays instead. The two can be combined.

Call flows are at Telephony → Call Flows.

Create a call flow

  1. Choose New call flow.
  2. If you manage several organizations, choose the Organization.
  3. Enter a Name, such as Night mode, and a Code index from 0 to 99. The index must be unique within the organization; it is the number dialled after the toggle code.
  4. Choose Create call flow. Veyra opens its page.
  5. Set the two destinations:
    • Normally, calls go to
    • While switched, calls go to Both offer the same kinds as an inbound route (extension, voicemail, IVR menu, ring group, queue, announcement and so on), plus Hang up.
  6. Optionally set a PIN of 4 to 10 digits, which a phone must enter before it can switch.
  7. Choose Save, then Deploy changes in the top bar.

A new call flow starts with both destinations set to hang up, so set them before you send calls to it.

Send calls into the call flow

A call flow only affects calls that are sent to it. Choose Call flow as the destination of:

  • an inbound route, for example your main number,
  • or anywhere else Veyra asks for a destination, such as an IVR menu key.

Switch it

Switching takes effect immediately. No deployment is needed.

  • In the list: turn the switch in the Switched column on or off. The Calls go to column shows where calls go right now.
  • On the call flow's page: Switch now, and Back to normal to return. The Right now panel shows the state, who switched it and when.
  • From a phone: dial the call-flow toggle feature code (*28 by default) followed by the index, for example *281. Dial it again to switch back. If the call flow has a PIN, the phone asks for it. The exact code is shown in the Phone code column.
  • With a lit button: program a busy lamp field (BLF) key with the same code on a phone (for example the front-office phone). The light is on while the call flow is switched, so staff can see the state at a glance.

Good to know

  • The Status column shows Ready, Disabled, or a count of problems. Open the call flow to see them: a destination that no longer exists, or the toggle feature code turned off at Feature Codes (the Phone code column then shows Code disabled).
  • Enabled off leaves the call flow out of the phone system, and routes that point at it are flagged.
  • Renaming a call flow does not change its internal name (the Context shown under Information) or its phone code.
  • A call flow that is still used by a route, menu, group or announcement cannot be deleted. Change those first.

guides.title: Dial by name
guides.summary: Let callers reach people and offices by spelling a name on the keypad.
guides.html:
The dial-by-name directory lets a caller spell a first or last name on the keypad, hear the extension, and be connected. Callers reach it from a menu (an IVR key) or an inbound route that points to it.

Everyone whose extension has a voicemail box is listed by themselves. On this page you add the other names callers might spell, such as Front office, Nurse or Attendance, and the operator for 0.

The page is under Telephony → Dial by Name.

Add a name

  1. Open Telephony → Dial by Name. If you manage several organizations, pick the Organization first.
  2. Choose Add a name.
  3. Name: what callers spell, for example Front office. Callers can spell the first or the last word. Use letters, digits, spaces and . ' & ( ) / -, up to 100 characters.
  4. Number: an extension, ring group or queue of the organization.
  5. Choose Add.
  6. Choose Deploy changes in the top bar.

To change a name, choose its row. To remove it, choose the bin icon. Both need a deployment.

Set the operator

In the Operator card, enter the Operator number: an extension, ring group or queue. A caller in the directory who presses 0 goes there. Leave it empty and 0 says goodbye. Choose Save, then deploy.

If something doesn't work

  • A person is missing from the directory: they are listed only when their extension has a voicemail box. Create one on the extension's Voicemail tab, or add them here.
  • Callers cannot reach the directory: point an IVR key or an inbound route at it.

guides.title: Set up conference rooms
guides.summary: Create a dial-in meeting room with optional PINs, see who is in it, and mute, remove or end from the web.

headings.title: Keys people press in the room
Watch and control a meeting from the web
Let someone run their own room

guides.html:
A conference room is a number people dial to talk together: a staff meeting, a parent conference with a teacher and an interpreter, a call with a vendor. Anyone who dials the room's number joins the others already there. Outside callers can join too, when an inbound route or a menu key points at the room.

Before you start

You need permission to change ring groups, queues and conference rooms. Organization and site administrators have it by default.

1. Create the room

  1. Open Telephony → Conference Rooms and choose New conference room.
  2. If you manage several organizations, choose the Organization.
  3. Enter a Name, for example Board room, and a Number. The number shares the numbering plan with extensions and groups, so it must be free.
  4. Choose Create room. Veyra opens the room's page.

2. Set PINs and options

  • Participant PIN: 4 to 10 digits that callers must enter to join. Leave it empty for an open room.
  • Administrator PIN: 4 to 10 digits. Someone who joins with it is the room's administrator and can use the administrator keys below. Once a PIN is set it is never shown again; type a new one to change it, or tick Remove the participant PIN / Remove the administrator PIN.
  • Participant limit: 0 for no limit, up to 500.
  • Hold music while waiting alone: a hold music set, or the built-in music.
  • Announce when participants join and leave.
  • Play hold music to a participant who is alone.
  • Participants wait until an administrator joins: the meeting starts when someone joins with the administrator PIN. This needs an administrator PIN; without one the room shows a warning.
  • Record the conference: the whole meeting is recorded. The recordings are listed under Call Recording with a Conference badge. See Record calls.
  • Enabled: a disabled room is left out of the phone system.

Choose Save, then Deploy changes in the top bar.

a line key (BLF) with the room's number lights while the room is in use.

Keys people press in the room

The In the room card on the room's page lists them:

KeyWhat it does
*1Mute or unmute yourself
*4 / *6Listening volume down / up
*7 / *9Talking volume down / up
*2Administrator: lock or unlock the room
*3Administrator: drop the last participant who joined
*8Administrator: mute or unmute everyone else

Watch and control a meeting from the web

While a meeting is going on, the Live card on the room's page lists everyone in the room, with Admin and Muted badges, and updates every few seconds. If you may change conference rooms you can:

  • Mute or Unmute one participant, and Remove them from the room.
  • Mute everyone else mutes every participant who did not join as an administrator; Unmute all undoes it.
  • Lock the room so nobody else can join, and Unlock it.
  • End the meeting: everyone in the room is disconnected (you confirm with End for everyone).
  • Start recording and Stop recording: a Recording badge shows while it runs, and the recording appears under Call Recording a few minutes after it stops. A room with Record the conference on always records, so it has no stop button. After you update Veyra, deploy changes once before recording a room this way.
  • Invite a number: enter an extension or outside number and choose Call. When they answer they join the room without the PIN, as a participant. The call follows the class of service of your own phone, so a number your phone may not dial is not reached. Emergency numbers are refused.

Each of these actions is written to the audit log. They apply at once and need no deployment.

Let someone run their own room

In Room owners on the room's page, add the phones of the people who run this room and choose Save owners. This applies at once. Those people add the Conference widget on My Phone and get the same live controls for their rooms, including invitations, without any administrator permission.

When it does not work

  • Callers are asked for a PIN you did not expect: the room has a participant PIN. Remove it or share it.
  • Everyone hears music and nobody can talk: Participants wait until an administrator joins is on and nobody has joined with the administrator PIN.
  • The Live card says the engine is unavailable: the telephony engine is not running or cannot report rooms. Check System → Telephony Engine.
  • An invited person hears a PIN prompt: changes have not been deployed since the update. Choose Deploy changes.
  • An invited number never rings: the number has no outbound route, or your phone's class of service does not allow it.
  • Deleting a room: routes, menus, groups and announcements that point at it must be changed first.

guides.title: Build a phone menu
guides.summary: Greet callers with a recording, send each key to the right place, and play announcements before a call goes on.

headings.title: 3. Decide what happens when callers press nothing or the wrong key

guides.html:
A phone menu (an IVR menu, or auto-attendant) answers a call with a recording such as "For attendance, press 1. For the front office, press 2." and sends the caller wherever the key they press leads. An announcement plays one recording, then sends the call on: a closure notice before the main menu, or "this call may be recorded" before a queue.

Before you start

  • You need permission to change IVR menus, announcements and prompts. Organization and site administrators have it by default.
  • Record or upload the greeting first. A menu without a prompt does not work. See Manage audio and hold music: you can record from any phone with *95.
  • Create the places the keys lead to first (extensions, ring groups, queues, voicemail boxes), so you can choose them.

1. Create the menu

  1. Open Telephony → IVR Menus and choose New IVR menu.
  2. If you manage several organizations, choose the Organization.
  3. Enter a Name, for example Main menu.
  4. Choose the Menu prompt, or leave Choose later.
  5. Choose Create menu. Veyra opens the menu's page.

2. Map the keys

Under Keys, every key from 0 to 9, * and # is listed. Choose Key 1: not mapped (and so on) to map a key, then choose where it goes:

DestinationSends the caller to
ExtensionOne phone
Voicemail of an extensionStraight to that person's voicemail greeting
Shared voicemail inboxA shared box, such as the attendance line
IVR menuAnother menu (a sub-menu)
Ring group / Call queueA team
AnnouncementA recording, then onwards
Conference roomA meeting room
Call flowA day/night switch
Fax to emailA fax inbox
Dial-by-name directoryCallers spell a name
Hang upEnds the call

Remove unmaps a key again. A key can be mapped only once.

Tick Callers may dial an extension number during the menu to let callers who know an extension dial it. Only extensions of this organization can be reached. A mapped key wins over an extension starting with the same digit, so with key 2 mapped, nobody can dial extension 2001 from the menu.

3. Decide what happens when callers press nothing or the wrong key

  • Wait for a key (seconds): 1 to 30, after the prompt ends. Callers may press a key while the prompt is still playing.
  • Attempts before giving up: 1 to 9, timeouts or wrong keys before the caller is sent on. The prompt plays again between attempts.
  • After too many timeouts: where callers who press nothing go. Send them to a person (for example the reception ring group) rather than Hang up: callers on old phones or who do not understand the menu end up here.
  • Invalid-key prompt: what callers hear after a wrong key. The default says "I'm sorry, that's not a valid extension".
  • After too many invalid keys: where they go then.

4. Save, deploy and connect

  1. Choose Save changes, then Deploy changes in the top bar.
  2. Point an inbound route at the menu so outside callers reach it (Telephony → Inbound Routes), or map a key of another menu to it.

The As deployed card shows the prompt, each key and the fallbacks as the phone system will use them.

Announcements

  1. Open Telephony → Announcements and choose New announcement.
  2. Enter a Name, choose the Recording to play (or Choose later), and choose Create announcement.
  3. On the announcement's page:
    • Callers may press any key to skip the recording.
    • Key that replays the recording: optional, 0–9, * or #.
    • Then send the call to: where the call goes after the recording.
  4. Choose Save, then Deploy changes.

Point a route, a menu key, a group's or queue's failover, or another announcement at it.

for a snow day or holiday closure, put an announcement in front of the main menu and switch between the two with a call flow, so the change is one key press on a phone. Call flows and time conditions are explained in their own guides.

When it does not work

  • Callers hear a fast busy tone: the menu has no prompt (No prompt in the list), or the announcement has no recording. Choose one and deploy.
  • A problems badge: read the list on the page. A destination may have been deleted, or the menu has no keys and direct dialling is off.
  • A key does nothing: the key is not mapped, or the change has not been deployed.
  • You cannot delete a menu or an announcement: routes, menus, groups and queues that point at it must be changed first.

guides.title: Who can call where (classes of service)
guides.summary: Limit what groups of phones may dial, such as local calls only for classrooms, while 911 always works.
guides.html:
A class of service is a set of permissions for a group of phones: which outbound routes they may use, which feature codes they may dial, and a few other limits. You create classes, then put extensions in them.

An extension without a class may do everything. Nothing is restricted until you create a class and assign it. Emergency routes always work for every class.

Classes of service are at Telephony → Classes of Service. Each organization has its own classes.

Plan first

Classes are built from your outbound routes, so split the routes the way you want to allow them. For example:

Outbound routeClassroomsStaffOffice
Local✓✓✓
Long distance✓✓
International✓

The office phones could simply have no class at all.

Create a class

  1. Choose New class.
  2. If you manage several organizations, choose the Organization.
  3. Enter a Name, such as Classrooms, and an optional Description.
  4. Under Outbound routes the class may use, tick the routes. Emergency routes are not listed because they are always allowed. With no route ticked, the phones can call extensions and 911 only.
  5. Every feature code: leave it on to allow every star code, or turn it off and tick the codes the class may dial.
  6. Set the other permissions:
SettingWhen ticked
Forwards may go to outside numbersPeople can forward their phone to a mobile or other outside number
Follow-me may ring outside numbersFollow-me can include outside numbers
May use intercomThe phone can make intercom calls that answer on the other phone's speaker
May send faxes from My PhonePeople can send faxes from the web
May listen to, whisper on and join calls (supervisor codes)The phone may use *222, *223 and *224 plus an extension. Off by default. Check your state's rules on call monitoring and consent before turning it on
Never monitoredNobody can listen to these phones' calls, with a supervisor code or from the web. Use it for counselors, nurses and others whose calls must stay private
  1. Outside calls at once (empty: no limit): the most outside calls the whole class may have at the same time, counted across all its phones (1 to 500). When the limit is reached, the next caller hears a busy signal.
  2. Choose Create class, then Deploy changes in the top bar.

Put phones in a class

Open an extension under Extensions and choose its Class of service, or set the class on an extension template so new extensions get it. Save and deploy.

The Also column of the list shows what differs from the defaults: No outside forwards, No outside follow-me, No intercom, No fax, Supervisor codes, Never monitored, and the limit of outside calls. The Extensions column shows how many extensions are in each class.

What people notice

  • Dialling a number whose route is not in their class: the call is refused with a short recorded message, and Call History shows it as refused.
  • Dialling a feature code their class does not allow: the code is refused.
  • Dialling 911 (or any number on an emergency route): always goes through.

Editing and deleting

Choose Edit on a class (or click its row), change it, and choose Save changes, then deploy.

When you add a new outbound route later, existing classes do not get it automatically. Edit each class that should use it.

A class that still has extensions cannot be deleted. Move them to another class (or to none) first.

guides.title: Block callers
guides.summary: Refuse calls from unwanted numbers, and optionally from callers who hide their number.

headings.title: Rules for blocked and hidden callers

guides.html:
The block list holds numbers your organization refuses. A call from a blocked number is refused on every inbound route of the organization, before any phone rings. Calls between your own extensions are not affected.

The list is at Telephony → Blocked Callers. If you manage several organizations, choose the Organization first: each has its own list.

Block a number

  1. Choose Block a number.
  2. Enter the Number exactly as the caller ID shows it, for example 5735551234. Spaces, dashes, dots and brackets are removed; the number must be 2 to 32 digits, optionally with a leading +.
  3. Optionally add a Note, such as why it is blocked.
  4. Choose Block.

The block takes effect at once. No deployment is needed.

The number must match the caller ID exactly as your carrier delivers it. 5735551234 does not block +15735551234. Look the call up in Call History to see the form your carrier uses, and if in doubt block both forms.

Block from a phone

Anyone allowed to dial these feature codes can manage the list from a desk phone:

Code (default)Does
*30Asks for a number and blocks it
*32Blocks the last outside caller who called this phone directly
*31Asks for a number and unblocks it

Numbers blocked from a phone appear in the list with From a phone in the Added column. The codes can be changed or turned off at Feature Codes, and limited with a class of service.

Import and export

  • Import takes a list with one number per line, optionally followed by a comma and a note (5735551234,Robocaller). A CSV exported from Veyra, or from FreePBX, works as is. Up to 5,000 lines at a time. Numbers already blocked keep their block and get the new note, and lines that are not valid numbers are listed as skipped.
  • Export CSV downloads the organization's list.

Rules for blocked and hidden callers

The Rules panel applies to the whole organization:

  • Block callers who withhold their number: also refuses callers whose number is anonymous, restricted, private or unavailable.
  • Blocked calls go to: what refused callers get. Hang up (the default) plays "the number you have dialled is not in service" and hangs up. You can instead send them somewhere, for example a voicemail box or an announcement.

Choose Save rules, then Deploy changes in the top bar. Unlike the numbers themselves, the rules need a deployment.

The panel also counts the Blocked numbers and Blocked calls (with how many were withheld numbers). The list shows how many calls each number made since it was blocked and when the last one was.

Unblock

Choose Unblock on the number's row and confirm. Calls from it reach the organization again at once.

If it does not work

  • A blocked number still gets through. Compare the caller ID in Call History with the number in the list, character for character, including any leading 1 or +.
  • Legitimate callers are refused. If Block callers who withhold their number is on, some callers (for example hospitals or other organizations' phone systems) hide their number. Turn it off, or send blocked calls to a voicemail box instead of hanging up.

guides.title: Manage audio and hold music
guides.summary: Record prompts from a phone, upload audio, add Veyra's built-in sounds, and build hold music sets.

headings.title: Record a prompt from a phone

guides.html:
Every recording callers hear lives in the organization's audio library: menu greetings, announcements, bells, voicemail greetings and hold music. You fill the library in three ways: record from a phone, upload a file, or copy one of Veyra's built-in sounds. Hold music sets then group music recordings into what callers hear on hold.

You need permission to change IVR menus, announcements and prompts (organization and site administrators by default).

Record a prompt from a phone
