A desk phone records clearer speech than most laptop microphones, and nothing has to be converted.

  1. From any phone, dial *95.
  2. After the tone, speak. Press # when you are done. A recording stops by itself after 5 seconds of silence or 5 minutes.
  3. The phone plays the recording back. Press 1 to keep it, 2 to listen again, or 3 to record it again.
  4. Open Telephony → Audio. The recording is listed under Recordings from phones with the time and the extension it came from. Use the play button to listen.
  5. Choose Name and keep, enter a Name (for example After-hours greeting) and optionally a Description, then Create prompt. Or discard it with the bin button.

The new prompt is now in the library list above and can be chosen in menus and announcements.

Upload a file

  1. On Telephony → Audio, choose Upload audio.
  2. Enter a Name and choose the Kind: Menu prompt, Bell, Announcement, Greeting or Hold music. The kind sorts the library; hold music sets offer recordings of the kind Hold music first.
  3. Optionally enter a Description, a Licence (where the rights come from, for example CC0 or own recording) and a Credit.
  4. Choose the Audio file and Upload.

Veyra accepts WAV files, and MP3, OGG, FLAC and M4A when ffmpeg is installed on the server. A file can be at most 5 minutes long. It is converted to the format phones play (8 kHz mono).

Built-in sounds

The Built-in sounds card lists bells, chimes, attention tones and hold music made by Veyra and free to use. Play one with its play button, and choose Add to library to copy it into the organization's library (with several organizations, first choose which one). After that, bell schedules, pages and menus can use it.

Change or replace a recording

Choose Edit next to a recording to change its Name or Description, or to Replace the audio with a new file. The new audio plays at once wherever the recording is used; menus and announcements keep pointing at it, and no deployment is needed for the replaced sound.

A recording that something still plays cannot be deleted: an IVR menu, an announcement, a call queue (its join or periodic announcement), a recording policy's announcement, a recorded page or bell, or a hold music set. The Used by column shows how many use it. If you try, the message lists each one by name; choose another recording there first.

to change a greeting that was recorded from a phone, record the new one with *95, name it, choose it as the menu's Menu prompt (or the announcement's Recording to play) and deploy.

Hold music sets

Callers on hold, waiting in a queue, waiting alone in a conference room, or ringing a ring group set to play music hear a hold music set. Anything without a set plays Veyra's built-in music, which needs no licence.

  1. Upload or add the music to the library first, with the kind Hold music.
  2. Open Telephony → Hold Music and choose New hold music set.
  3. Enter a Name and optionally a Description.
  4. Choose the Source:
    • Recordings from the audio library: choose each recording and click Add, up to 50, and order them with the arrows. Tick Offer every recording, not only those marked as hold music to see other kinds. Tick Shuffle to play them in random order.
    • An internet radio stream: enter the Stream address (an http:// or https:// address of an MP3, AAC or Ogg station). The server needs ffmpeg. The recordings you add are played as a fallback while the station cannot be reached.
  5. Choose Create set, then Deploy changes in the top bar.

Then choose the set where it should play:

  • for calls put on hold, as the organization's default set on its page under Directory → Organizations;
  • for a queue or ring group, in its Hold music set field;
  • for a conference room, in Hold music while waiting alone.
commercial music and radio stations played to callers usually need a public performance licence, and a station may also need to give permission. Veyra's built-in music and Creative Commons or public-domain recordings do not. The licence you enter with each upload is shown in the set.

A set that a queue, ring group or organization uses cannot be deleted until they are changed. The recordings stay in the library when a set is deleted.

When it does not work

  • No recording appears under Recordings from phones: the recording was not kept (press 1 after listening), or it was made in another organization (choose the organization filter).
  • The upload is refused: the file is longer than 5 minutes, too large, or in a format the server cannot convert without ffmpeg. Convert it to WAV and try again.
  • A set shows a warning: it has no recordings, a recording's file is missing, or ffmpeg is not installed for a stream.
  • Callers still hear the old music: deploy the changes.

guides.title: Emergency calling (911)
guides.summary: Set up 911 so it dials directly, sends the right number and location, alerts people on site, and reaches the caller on a callback.
guides.html:
Emergency calling is safety-critical. Veyra checks your configuration against its own list, but it does not certify that 911 works. You must test it with your carrier and make sure you meet the laws that apply to you. This guide is not legal advice.

In the United States, two federal rules apply to phone systems with many lines (Kari's Law and RAY BAUM'S Act):

  • People must be able to dial 911 directly, without an outside-line prefix such as 9.
  • When someone dials 911, the system must notify someone on site (a front office or security desk).
  • The 911 call must carry a dispatchable location: the street address plus details such as the building, floor or room.

State laws may add requirements, and other countries have their own emergency numbers and rules.

Veyra handles this in four places. Work through them in order, then check the result at System → Emergency Calling.

1. Sites: address and emergency number

Open Directory → Sites and, for each site (each campus or building with its own address):

  • Enter the full civic address: Street, City, State or region, Postal code.
  • Enter the Emergency caller ID number: the number the 911 center sees and calls back. This is often called the ELIN. It must be one of your numbers, and your carrier must have it registered with this site's address in their E911 service.

Ask your carrier to register each site's emergency number and address before going further. Veyra cannot do that part.

2. Extensions: site and location

On each extension's page under Extensions:

  • Choose its Site and, where you have them, its Building.
  • Fill in Location (dispatchable), such as Room 101, first floor.
  • Leave Emergency caller ID number empty to use the site's number. Fill it in only when this phone needs a different emergency number (for example a building with its own registered number). The extension's number wins over the site's.

3. The emergency route

Open Telephony → Outbound Routes and choose New outbound route (platform administrators only):

  1. Name: such as Emergency.
  2. Tick Emergency route. Emergency routes are always tried before every other route, cannot be moved below them, and work for every phone whatever its class of service.
  3. Dial patterns: add 911 and, if your carrier supports test calls, 933, with no prefix. If people are used to dialling 9 for an outside line, also add a pattern with Prefix (stripped) 9 and Match 911, so 9911 reaches 911 too.
  4. Trunks: add your main trunk and, if you have one, a second trunk as a backup. The backup is tried when the first trunk is unavailable.
  5. Caller ID number: optional, used for phones that have no emergency number from steps 1 and 2.
  6. Create route, then Deploy changes in the top bar.

The Outbound Routes page warns you when there is no enabled emergency route, and when extensions have no emergency caller ID.

One route per site (optional)

If your sites use different trunks, create one emergency route per site and choose the site under For the phones of. A site's route is tried first for that site's phones and passes other phones on to the next emergency route.

Always keep one emergency route for Every site as well. Routes bound to a site are tried before it.

Keep a line free for 911

On each trunk the emergency route uses, set Maximum channels to the number of calls your carrier allows and Channels kept for emergency calls to at least 1 (see Connect a SIP trunk). Ordinary calls then never use the last channel, so a 911 call can get out even when every other line is busy.

4. On-site notification and callback

At System → Emergency Calling, choose Open on a site. (Changing these settings needs the emergency-calling management permission.)

  • This address is registered with the carrier's E911 service for the ELIN above: tick it once the carrier has confirmed. Your name and the date are recorded.
  • Responder extension: the phone that rings when the 911 center calls back and Veyra cannot tell who made the call, or the callback window has passed. The list shows the site's own extensions (all of the organization's extensions when none belongs to the site).
  • Callback window (minutes): how long after a 911 call a call to the site's emergency number rings the phone that dialled 911 (1 to 1440, 30 by default).
  • Notify by email: one address per line. Email must be set up first, in the Email delivery card under System → Settings.
  • Ring these extensions: extension numbers, separated by commas (up to 20). These phones ring when someone dials 911, show the caller's extension as the name, and hear it read out.
  • Play a recorded page: a recorded page (see Send a page) played into its zones when someone at this site dials 911, for example an alert on the front office speakers. Only pages of the site's organization that have a recording are listed; No page plays nothing.
  • Send the emergency.call webhook: for your own systems, through the webhooks set up in Veyra.

Choose Save, then Deploy changes in the top bar if it appears (the responder and callback window are part of the phone system's configuration).

On-site notification by phone, email or paging is not a life-safety mass notification system. Do not rely on it as one.

5. Test

  1. Test the notification now sends the real notifications (email, ringing phones, the recorded page, webhook), marked as a test with the number 933. Check that everyone received them. The notification check passes once a test reached at least one recipient.
  2. Arrange a test call with your carrier (933 where they support it, or a scheduled 911 test). Ask the 911 center to read back the number and address they see.
  3. Under Carrier test call, type what they read back in Result and choose Record as passed or Record as failed.

Repeat the carrier test at least once a year, and after any change to trunks, sites or emergency numbers.

Readiness

The Sites table shows each site as ready or how many checks are missing. Open a site to see every check:

  • An enabled emergency route with a trunk reaches this site
  • Every emergency trunk keeps a channel free for emergency calls (advice only; it does not stop a site being ready)
  • The site has an emergency caller ID (ELIN or registered DID)
  • The site has a civic address
  • The address is attested as registered with the carrier's E911 service
  • Every extension of the site has a location (building or floor/room)
  • On-site notification recipients are set
  • The notification was tested
  • A test call with the carrier succeeded within the last year

Ready means Veyra's checks pass. It does not mean the carrier delivers the right address: only the carrier test shows that.

What happens on a 911 call

  • The call goes out through the first matching emergency route, ignoring any class of service and channel limit, and rings for up to 120 seconds.
  • The number sent is the extension's Emergency caller ID number, else the site's, else the usual outgoing caller ID. Hiding the number (such as *67) has no effect on an emergency call.
  • The notifications from step 4 go out, and the call is listed under Emergency calls with the caller's extension, the number dialled, the location and who was notified. Test notifications are marked test, real calls live.
  • When the 911 center calls the emergency number back within the callback window, the phone that made the call rings, even if the number has no inbound route of its own. After the window (or when Veyra cannot tell who called), the Responder extension rings. Without a responder, the number's normal inbound route answers, and a number without an inbound route is not answered, so set a responder.

If something is missing

  • "No enabled emergency route": create the route in step 3, or turn it back on.
  • Extensions missing a location: the readiness check lists up to ten of them; fill in their Location (dispatchable) or Building.
  • The notification test fails: check that email is set up, and that the extensions listed under Ring these extensions exist in the site's organization.
  • The 911 center sees the wrong address: the address registered with the carrier for that number is wrong. Correct it with the carrier, then test again.

guides.title: Record calls
guides.summary: Choose which calls are recorded and for how long, record a call on demand, and listen to recordings with every playback audited.

headings.title: Keep a recording past its retention date

guides.html:
Veyra records nothing until you say so. A recording policy says which calls of an organization are recorded, what callers hear first, and how long the recordings are kept. Recordings can also be started during a single call. Every time someone listens to or downloads a recording, it is written to the audit log.

recording calls is regulated. Some states require that everyone on the call agrees. Check your district's or company's policy and the law before you turn recording on, and play an announcement to callers.

Who can do what

PermissionLets someoneBy default
View what calls are recordedSee the Policies tabOrganization and site administrators, read-only users
Change what calls are recordedAdd, change and remove policiesOrganization administrators
Listen to and download call recordingsThe Recordings tab, for the whole organizationOrganization administrators
Listen to recordings of your own callsThe Recordings tab, for calls of their own extensionsNobody
Download many recordings at once with a spreadsheet of the callsExport on the Recordings tabOrganization administrators
Hold, release and delete call recordingsHold, Release and DeleteOrganization administrators
Start and stop recording a call in progressRecord on Active CallsOrganization and site administrators

Users can also be allowed to play recordings of their own calls on My Phone: on the organization's page under Directory → Organizations, switch on Users may play recordings of their own calls.

1. Add a recording announcement

Record or upload a short recording such as "This call may be recorded for quality purposes", as described in Manage audio and hold music.

2. Add a policy

  1. Open Telephony → Call Recording, the Policies tab, and choose New policy.
  2. If you manage several organizations, choose the Organization.
  3. Enter a Name, for example Front office lines.
  4. Under Directions, tick which calls: Inbound (from outside), Outbound (to outside), Internal (phone to phone).
  5. Under Which calls, choose:
    • Every call of the organization in these directions, or
    • Only calls of the phones, groups, queues and numbers chosen below, then pick the Phones, Ring groups, Queues and Inbound numbers (DIDs).
  6. Choose the Announcement callers hear before the call connects.
  7. Set Keep recordings (days): 1 to 3650. Recordings are deleted after this unless held.
  8. Leave Enabled on and choose Add policy.
  9. Choose Deploy changes in the top bar. Recording starts with the next call after the deployment.

The Notes box under the list warns about policies that record nothing (no direction ticked, or nothing chosen), and about inbound recording without an announcement.

To stop recording, edit the policy and switch off Enabled, or remove it, then deploy. Recordings already made are kept until their retention date.

Record one call on demand

  • From a phone: during a call, press *1. A beep confirms the recording has started. Press *1 again to stop it. The extension's class of service can forbid this; the phone then plays an error tone.
  • From the web: on Active Calls, choose Record on the call, and Stop recording to end it. See Watch live calls.

On-demand recordings are kept for 90 days.

Conference rooms with Record the conference on are recorded as well; they appear with a Conference badge and Whole room as the other party.

Listen to recordings

  1. Open the Recordings tab. To narrow the list, choose an Organization (when you manage several), a From and To date, a Direction, or a Number or name.
  2. Each recording shows the call's time, direction, From, To, Length and Deleted on (its retention date, or Held).
  3. Choose Listen. The player plays the recording in the browser; Download MP3 saves a file any audio player opens, named with the call's date, time, direction and numbers.

Recordings appear about a minute after a recorded call ends. You can also open a call in Call History and play its recording there.

Every listening and download is written to the audit log with who did it.

Export recordings

Use this for a records request, or to keep recordings outside Veyra.

  1. On the Recordings tab, set the filters so the list shows what you need.
  2. Choose Export. The window shows how many recordings match and about how large the file is.
  3. Choose the Audio format. MP3 plays in any audio player. Ogg Opus is the stored file, which is smaller and faster to export but does not open in every player.
  4. Choose Download ZIP.

The ZIP holds one audio file per recording, named like 2026-10-30_1432_inbound_5551234_to_1001.mp3 in the organization's time zone, and recordings.csv, which opens in a spreadsheet. Each row names its file and gives the call's times, direction, outcome, numbers, caller name, dialled number, who answered, trunk, queue or ring group, ring and talk seconds, policy, organization and whether it is held.

  • One export holds at most 2000 recordings or 20 GB; for more, export one date range at a time.
  • Exported files are not encrypted, unlike the recordings on the server, and the retention dates and audit log no longer apply to them. Keep them somewhere appropriate.
  • The export is written to the audit log with who did it and which recordings it held.
  • If a recording could not be read, its row in recordings.csv says so in the status column. Check that column after a records request.

The Call History CSV has a recording_ref column, which matches recording_ref in recordings.csv.

Keep a recording past its retention date

When a recording is needed for an investigation or a complaint, choose Hold. A held recording is not deleted until someone chooses Release; after that it is deleted at its retention date like any other.

Delete a recording

To remove a recording before its retention date, choose Delete on its row and confirm. The audio is removed at once and cannot be brought back; the call stays in the call history, and the deletion is written to the audit log. A held recording has no Delete button: choose Release first.

Tick Show deleted to list deleted recordings too. They show Deleted with the date instead of Listen.

When it does not work

  • No recordings appear: check the policy is enabled, covers the call's direction and the phones or numbers involved, and that you deployed after adding it.
  • The policy shows a note: read it; a policy with no direction or nothing chosen records nothing.
  • The browser cannot play the recording: use Download MP3.
  • *1 gives an error tone: the phone's class of service does not allow on-demand recording.

guides.title: Watch live calls
guides.summary: See the calls in progress, hang one up, record it, or listen in, whisper and join as a supervisor.
guides.html:
Telephony → Active Calls lists every call that is ringing or up right now: the extension, who called whom, the state and how long it has lasted. The list updates by itself every few seconds; Refresh updates it at once.

Who can do what

PermissionLets someoneBy default
View active callsSee the listOrganization and site administrators, technicians, read-only users
Hang up calls in progressHang upOrganization and site administrators, technicians
Start and stop recording a call in progressRecordOrganization and site administrators
Listen to, whisper on and join calls in progress (supervisor)Supervise…Organization and site administrators

Platform administrators see every call. Everyone else sees the calls of extensions in the organizations they manage; a call leg Veyra cannot match to one of those extensions, such as the trunk side of an outside call, is shown only to platform administrators.

Read the list

  • Extension: the phone in the call, with the person's name. A leg on a trunk shows the phone system's name for the trunk instead.
  • From and To: the numbers.
  • State: Ring or Ringing while it rings, Up while people talk.
  • Channel: the phone system's name for this side of the call; support may ask for it.

A call between two phones shows up twice, once for each side.

Hang up a call

Choose Hang up, then Hang up again to confirm (or Keep to cancel). This ends that side of the call; the phone system clears the other side. Use it for a call stuck on a line or a phone left off the hook.

Record a call

Choose Record to start recording the call, and Stop recording to stop. The recording is filed with the call when it ends and appears under Call Recording. See Record calls.

A call that is already being recorded, by a recording policy or from a phone, shows a Recording badge instead. Only a recording started here can be stopped here. A call can be recorded from this page once: after Stop recording, starting again is refused.

Supervise a call

A supervisor can hear a call without being heard, coach the staff member without the caller hearing, or join the call.

  1. Find the call and open Supervise… next to it.
  2. Choose Listen, Whisper to the user or Join the call.
  3. Your own desk phone rings: the first enabled extension assigned to you. If you have several extensions, pick the phone that should ring in Supervise from above the list first. Answer it:
    • Listen: you hear both sides; nobody hears you.
    • Whisper to the user: the staff member hears you, the caller does not.
    • Join the call: both sides hear you.
  4. Hang up your phone to stop.

Every supervision session is written to the audit log: who, which call, which mode and from which phone.

Supervisors can do the same from a phone, without the web, with the default codes *222 (listen), *223 (whisper) or *224 (join) followed by the extension. That needs a class of service with May listen to, whisper on and join calls (supervisor codes).

Beep and protection

  • On the organization's page under Directory → Organizations, Beep when a supervisor listens in plays a short beep to both sides when supervision starts. Some states require that everyone on a call knows it is being monitored.
  • A class of service with Never monitored protects its phones: nobody can listen to, whisper on or join their calls, for example a counselor's or the nurse's phone.

When it does not work

  • "Live call data is not available": the telephony engine is not running or cannot report calls. Check System → Telephony Engine.
  • "You have no phone to listen on": you have no enabled extension assigned to your user. Ask an administrator to assign one.
  • "…class of service does not allow monitoring": the phone is protected with Never monitored.
  • "That is the call on your own phone": you cannot supervise your own call.
  • Your phone does not ring: check that your extension is registered (Telephony → Registrations).

guides.title: Call history and reports
guides.summary: Look up any call, export the history, build your own reports and have them emailed on a schedule.
guides.html:
Veyra keeps a record of every call: who called whom, who answered, how long it rang and how long people talked. Call History finds single calls, for example when a parent says nobody answered. Reports adds them up: busy hours, missed calls per office, how long queue callers wait.

Who can do what

PermissionLets someoneBy default
View the call history of the organizationOpen Call HistoryOrganization and site administrators, technicians, read-only users
Export the call history as CSVExport CSV on Call HistoryOrganization administrators
View call reportsOpen Reports, run and export reportsOrganization and site administrators, read-only users
Save, share and schedule reportsSave report…, Send now, deleteOrganization and site administrators

Find a call

  1. Open Telephony → Call History.
  2. Choose the period: Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, Last 90 days, or Custom range with two dates.
  3. Narrow it down with the search box (a number, a name or an extension), All directions (Internal, Inbound, Outbound), Any length (Talked 30 s or more, Talked 1 min or more, Talked 5 min or more, Talked 15 min or more), Recorded or not (Recorded, Not recorded) and All outcomes:
OutcomeMeans
AnsweredSomeone picked up
MissedIt rang and nobody answered
BusyThe other side was busy
FailedThe call could not be placed
VoicemailIt ended in voicemail
AbandonedThe caller hung up while waiting, for example in a queue
Blocked callerThe number is on the blocked list
Not allowedThe phone's class of service does not allow the number
  1. Click a call to see the details: direction and trunk, the number dialled (DID), who answered, ringing and talking time, and each leg of the call as the phone system saw it. If the call was recorded (a record icon in the list) and you may listen to recordings, the recording plays here.

Calls appear a few seconds after they end. The relative periods are fixed when the page opens; Refresh brings them up to now.

Export CSV downloads the calls that match the current filters, all of them (talk time and recording included), up to 100,000 rows.

Veyra keeps the call history for 400 days by default. A platform administrator can change that under Settings, in the Retention card.

The reports overview

Telephony → Reports, Overview tab, summarises a period (Last 7 days to Last 365 days, or Custom range), optionally for one organization:

  • Calls, Missed, Average ring / talk, and the share of inbound calls answered within 20 seconds.
  • Calls per day by direction, and Busiest hours by weekday and hour.
  • Extensions: answered, missed and talk time per extension.
  • Trunks: inbound and outbound calls per carrier connection, and Most at once, the most calls up at the same time. Compare it with the number of channels your carrier sells you.
  • Queues: callers, answered, Hung up waiting, Average wait, Answered within 20 s, Left by the menu (callers who used the break-out menu), and per agent the calls answered and time logged in and paused.

Days and hours are in the organization's time zone.

Build a report

On the Build tab:

  1. Choose the Period, from Today to This year, or Custom dates.
  2. Choose Group by, for example Day, Hour of day, Called extension, Number dialled (DID), Queue or Caller number. Add Then by and And by for up to three levels.
  3. Tick the Measures: Calls, Answered, Missed, Voicemail, Answer rate, Average ring, Total ring, Average talk, Total talk, Answered within service level (then set the Service level (seconds)).
  4. Open Filters to include only some calls: directions, outcomes, extensions (either side of the call), numbers dialled, queues, ring groups, trunks, Caller number contains, At least this much talk (seconds), and Business hours: inside or outside the hours and holidays of a time condition you choose.
  5. Choose Show as (Table, Bars and table, Line and table), the sort order and Show at most (rows) (up to 5000).
  6. Choose Run. Under the chart, Chart picks which measure the chart shows; the table always shows them all, with the totals below.

Export CSV downloads the result.

Save and email a report

  1. On the Build tab choose Save report….
  2. Enter a Name and optionally a Description.
  3. Shared with the organization: on, everyone who may see reports can open it; off, only you and report editors.
  4. Switch on Email it on a schedule to send the result as a CSV: How often (Every day, Every week, Every month), At (the hour, in the organization's time zone), On (weekday) or On day (day of the month; a shorter month sends on its last day), and Email to, one address per line, up to 20.
  5. Choose Save.

The Saved tab lists the reports with their schedule, the next and last email, and any sending error. Open loads a report into the builder; save it again to change it, or tick Save as a new report. Send now emails a scheduled report at once.

the CSV contains call data, including phone numbers. Send it only to people allowed to see it.

Emails need outgoing mail to be set up in the Email delivery card under Settings. Without it, sending fails and the error shows in the Last sent column.

When it does not work

  • A call is missing: widen the period, clear the filters, and check the organization filter. Calls appear only after they end.
  • No Export CSV button: you do not have the permission to export the call history.
  • A report covers at most 400 days: shorten the period.
  • A scheduled report was not received: look at Last sent on the Saved tab, check the mail settings, and try Send now.

guides.title: Set up paging zones and overhead speakers
guides.summary: Group your overhead speakers and Poly phones into paging zones that anyone allowed can page by dialling a number.

headings.title: Make the phones hear the zone
Page a zone from a phone

guides.html:
A paging zone is one area that hears a page together: a building, a wing, a floor, the gym, outdoors. Each zone ties together two things:

  • the multicast address your overhead speakers already listen to (Algo, CyberData, AND and similar speakers), and
  • the Poly group number that Poly desk phones listen to for the same area.

Poly phones only play Poly group pages, and speakers only play plain multicast. Veyra sends every page in both formats at the same moment, so the phones and the speakers in a zone play it together.

Once a zone has a number, anyone allowed can pick up a phone, dial that number and talk. To combine several zones, or to play a recording (a bell, a chime, a lockdown drill message), create a page on top of the zones: see Create and send pages.

Paging over the phone system is not a life-safety notification system. Use it for announcements, bells and drills. It does not replace your fire alarm or a certified mass notification system.

Zones are listed under Telephony → Paging Zones.

Before you start

  • On each speaker, note the multicast address and port it plays (on an Algo or CyberData speaker, the multicast zone settings on its web page). Speakers in the same zone share one address and port.
  • Decide which Poly group number (1 to 24) each zone uses. Group 25 is Poly's emergency group.
  • You need permission to change paging (paging.write). Organization administrators have it.

Create a zone

  1. Choose New paging zone.
  2. Fill in the form:
FieldWhat to enter
NameWhat people call the area, for example Building A. Required.
Site (optional)The site the zone belongs to, shown in the list.
Speakers' multicast addressThe address the speakers listen to, between 224.0.0.0 and 239.255.255.255, for example 239.1.2.10. Required.
Speakers' portThe speakers' port, 1024 to 65535. Default 5004.
Poly group number1 to 24 for normal zones; 25 is Poly's emergency group. Each zone of an organization needs its own group number.
KindNormal, Priority (interrupts calls), or Emergency (group 25). Priority and emergency pages play on Poly phones even during a call.
Poly paging address / Poly paging portOne address and port that all Poly phones of the organization listen on. Leave the default (224.0.1.116, port 5001) unless your network needs another.
CodecG.711 µ-law (default) works everywhere. G.722 (wideband) sounds better if all your speakers and phones support it.
Number to dial (optional)The number people dial to page this zone live. It comes from the same numbering plan as extensions, groups and pages, so it cannot be in use already.
Longest page (seconds)5 to 600, default 120. The page is cut off after this.
Who may page itSee below.
DescriptionOptional notes.
EnabledA disabled zone is left out of the phones' paging groups.
  1. Choose Create zone.
  2. A Changes not yet deployed note appears on the page. Use Deploy changes in the top bar so the phone system learns the zone's number. Phones get the zone itself at their next provisioning check.

Who may page a zone

Who may page it decides which phones can dial the zone's number:

  • Everyone in the organization: any phone of the organization.
  • Listed phones only: only the phones you add under Phones allowed to page. With nobody listed, nobody can page the zone from a phone, and the zone shows a warning.
  • Only from Veyra (interface, bells, API): no phone can dial it. Pages that include the zone can still be started from Veyra, by a bell schedule or by another system.

Make the phones hear the zone

Poly phones listen to a zone only when their device profile subscribes them to it. Open Device Profiles, choose the profile your phones use, and pick the zones its phones should hear. The Profiles column of the zones list shows which profiles use each zone. Phones pick up the change at their next provisioning check.

Speakers need no change in Veyra: they already listen to their multicast address.

Page a zone from a phone

Dial the zone's number from a phone that is allowed to page it. After the short tone, speak; hang up to end the page. A phone that is not allowed hears an "invalid" message. The page stops by itself after the zone's Longest page time.

Reading the list

The Status column shows Ready, Disabled, or the first problem found, for example:

  • Only members may page this zone, and it has none. Add phones, or choose another Who may page it.
  • Zones of this organization use different Poly paging addresses or ports. Poly phones listen on one address, so give every zone of the organization the same Poly paging address and port.
  • Another organization pages the same multicast address and port. On a shared network, both organizations' speakers would play each other's pages. Give one of them another address.
  • Poly phones use group 25 for emergency pages. An Emergency zone should use Poly group 25.

Delete a zone

Use the bin icon on the zone's row. A zone that a device profile still uses cannot be deleted: remove it from the profiles first.

If something doesn't work

  • Speakers play but Poly phones do not: check that the phones' device profile subscribes them to the zone, and that the phones have checked in since.
  • Phones play but speakers do not: compare the Speakers' multicast address and port with the speaker's own settings. Multicast must be allowed between the server and the speakers on your network.
  • "That number is already used": another extension, group, page or zone has that number. Choose another.
  • "Another zone of this organization already uses that Poly group number": each zone needs its own group number.

guides.title: Create and send pages
guides.summary: Combine paging zones into pages such as an all-call, give them a recording, and start them from a phone, from Veyra, from a bell or from another system.
guides.html:
A page is a named announcement into one or more paging zones. It carries either:

  • live audio: whoever dials the page's number talks, as on an intercom, or
  • a recording: a bell, a chime or a spoken message from the audio library, played into the zones when the page is started.

Typical pages are an All call over every zone, Building A and B for two buildings, or a Fire drill recording. Pages are listed under Telephony → Pages.

Paging over the phone system is not a life-safety notification system. The alert tones are meant for drills and attention, not as a replacement for a fire alarm.

Before you start

  • Create the zones first, under Paging Zones.
  • For a page with a recording, add the recording to the audio library under Audio. The Audio page also offers built-in bells, chimes and alert tones that you can add to the library.

Create a page

  1. Choose New page.
  2. Fill in the form:
FieldWhat to enter
NameFor example All call. Required, and unique in the organization.
Number to dial (optional)The number phones dial to start the page. Leave it blank for a page that is only started from Veyra, a bell or the API. It shares the numbering plan with extensions, groups and zones.
ZonesTick every zone the page reaches (up to 25).
AudioLeave Live: the caller's voice, or choose a recording. Only a page with a recording can be started from Veyra, by a bell schedule or by another system.
Repeat the recording1 to 5 times. Only with a recording.
PriorityNormal, Priority (interrupts calls on Poly phones) or Emergency.
Longest page (seconds)5 to 600, default 120.
Who may start it from a phoneEveryone in the organization, Listed phones only (add them under Phones allowed to start it), or Only from Veyra (interface, bells, API).
DescriptionOptional; shown under the name in the list.
Play a tone before the pageOn by default: a short tone warns people before the page starts.
EnabledA disabled page cannot be started.
  1. Choose Create page.
  2. If the page has a number, use Deploy changes in the top bar so phones can dial it.

Start a page

  • From a phone: dial the page's number. For a live page, speak after the tone and hang up when you are done. For a page with a recording, you hear a short beep and can hang up: the recording plays into the zones by itself. A phone that is not allowed to start the page hears an "invalid" message.
  • From Veyra: Send now on the page's row (shown for pages with a recording, to people allowed to send pages). The recording plays into the zones at once.
  • From a bell schedule: see Ring bells from a calendar.
  • From another system: a door controller, a building-management system or a script can start a recorded page through Veyra's API with an integration token that may Start pages. Tokens are created under System → Integrations. A device with a relay or a SIP line can also simply dial the page's number.

Phones and speakers in each zone play the page together.

Recent pages

The Recent pages card lists the last pages sent, with the zones, how each was started (from a phone, the interface, a bell or the API), who started it, and whether it started or failed. Entries are kept for 90 days by default; a platform administrator can change that on the Retention card under Settings.

Reading the list

The Status column shows Ready, Disabled, or the first problem found:

  • No zones: the page reaches nothing. Tick at least one zone.
  • A zone of this page is disabled. Turn the zone back on, or remove it from the page.
  • Only members may start this page, and it has none. Add phones, or change Who may start it from a phone.
  • The recording no longer exists. Choose another recording.

Send now answers This page plays live audio; dial its number from a phone to page for a page without a recording.

Delete a page

Use the bin icon on the page's row, then deploy the changes so phones no longer reach its number. Bell schedules that use the page stop ringing it.

guides.title: Ring bells from a calendar
guides.summary: Let a Google Calendar or any iCal calendar ring your school bells through the paging speakers.

headings.title: If a bell does not ring

guides.html:
Veyra rings bells from a calendar you already keep. You put the bell times in a calendar (for example a Google Calendar called Bell schedule, with an event for each period). Veyra checks the calendar every few minutes, and when an event starts (or ends, or both, as you choose) it plays a recorded page, such as a school bell, into the paging zones.

Changing the schedule then means editing the calendar: a late-start day, an assembly schedule or a holiday is just different events.

It takes three pieces:

  1. a page with a recording: the bell sound and the zones it plays in (see Create and send pages),
  2. a calendar in Veyra, linked to your calendar, and
  3. a bell schedule that connects the two.
Bells over the phone system are not a life-safety notification system. Use them for class changes and drills, not as a replacement for a fire alarm.

1. Make the bell page

Create a page with the zones that should hear the bell and a recording as its Audio, for example the built-in school bell (add it to your library from Audio first). Give it no number if only the bells should start it, and choose Only from Veyra (interface, bells, API) under Who may start it from a phone.

2. Add the calendar

You need the calendar's iCal address.

  • Google Calendar: in Google Calendar's settings, open the calendar and copy its Secret address in iCal format. It ends in basic.ics. Anyone with this address can read the calendar, so treat it like a password.
  • Other calendars: any iCal (.ics) feed works: Microsoft 365 published calendars, school information systems, and so on.

Then, under Telephony → Calendars:

  1. Choose Add calendar.
  2. Enter a Name, for example Bell schedule.
  3. Paste the Feed address. It must start with https://, http:// or webcal://. The address is stored encrypted and never shown again; the list shows only the server's name.
  4. Check every (minutes): 1 to 60, default 3.
  5. Time zone: leave it empty to use the calendar's own. Enter a name such as America/Chicago only for feeds that carry no time zone.
  6. Choose Add calendar. It is fetched within a minute.

The list shows when each calendar was Checked, how many Events (48 h) it has in the next two days (choose the number to see them), how many Bell schedules use it, and its Status. Fetch now checks it at once.

Recurring events (every school day at 8:05) work. Veyra reads the next two days of events at every check.

3. Create the bell schedule

Under Telephony → Bell Schedules:

  1. Choose New bell schedule.
  2. Fill in the form:
FieldWhat to enter
NameFor example Class periods.
CalendarThe calendar from step 2.
Page to ringThe bell page. Only pages with a recording are offered.
Events to ringWhich events ring, by their title. * (the default) rings every event. Bell:* rings only events whose title starts with Bell:. Upper and lower case do not matter.
RingWhen an event starts, When an event ends, or At start and end.
Late tolerance (seconds)0 to 900, default 90. If the server was busy or restarting, a bell up to this late is still rung; a later one is skipped rather than rung at the wrong time.
Include all-day eventsOff by default, so a holiday marked as an all-day event does not ring a bell at midnight.
EnabledTurn it off to pause the bells, for example over the summer.
  1. Choose Create schedule.

Each event rings once at each time chosen under Ring. Veyra checks for due bells every few seconds.

Check it

  • The Next ring column shows the next event that will ring and when.
  • Ring now plays the page at once, to test the sound and the zones.
  • History shows the last 50 rings of the schedule, each with its event, when it was due and whether it started or failed.
  • The Status column shows Ready, Disabled or the first problem, for example The calendar could not be fetched, The page has no recording; bells need one or The page is disabled.

If a bell does not ring

  • The calendar shows an error: open the calendar, paste the address again and save. For Google, make sure you copied the secret iCal address, not the public one, and that it has not been reset in Google Calendar since.
  • The bell rings at the wrong hour: the feed has no time zone; set Time zone on the calendar.
  • No events in the next 48 hours: choose the number in Events (48 h) to see what Veyra read. Check the event titles against Events to ring.
  • Ring now works but the scheduled bell does not: check that both the calendar and the schedule are enabled, and that the event is not an all-day event.

Removing things

  • Deleting a bell schedule keeps the calendar and the page.
  • Removing a calendar also removes the bell schedules that use it. Your calendar itself is not touched.

guides.title: Show messages on AND clocks
guides.summary: Send text messages and alerts to Advanced Network Devices (AND) IP clocks and signs, now, later or with the bells.

headings.title: 2. Describe how a clock takes a message (Clock Delivery)

guides.html:
If your buildings have Advanced Network Devices (AND) IP clocks or message signs, the optional AND Clock Messages module lets Veyra put text on them: to every clock, to a group such as a building, or to one clock; now or at a set time; and automatically when a bell rings (for example Period 2).

The module is not part of every installation. Install it only where these clocks exist.

Clock messages are not a life-safety notification system. Use them for information and drills alongside your fire alarm, not instead of it.

Install the module

  1. Open System → Module Manager.
  2. Find AND Clock Messages and choose Install, then Enable if it is not enabled yet.
  3. The module adds four pages to the Modules menu: Clock Messages, Clocks, Clock Bell Messages and Clock Delivery.

Organization administrators can manage everything; site administrators can send messages; technicians and read-only users can look.

1. Prepare the clocks

On each clock's own web page:

  • Turn on Allow inline text commands with InformaCast (under the clock's server settings). Veyra sets colour and flashers with these commands; without the setting they appear as text on the clock.
  • Note the clock's IP address (a DHCP reservation keeps it stable) and its HTTP control password, if one is set.

2. Describe how a clock takes a message (Clock Delivery)

AND does not publish a way for other systems to send messages, so Veyra copies what the clock's own web page does. You capture that once:

  1. On a computer on the clocks' network, open one clock's web page and go to the page that sends a text message.
  2. Press F12 to open the browser's developer tools and choose the Network tab.
  3. Send a short test message from the clock's page.
  4. Click the request that appeared (usually a POST). Note the method, the path (the part of the address after the clock's address), the request body (Payload) and whether the browser asked for a user name and password.
  5. In Veyra, open Clock Delivery and choose Add. Enter the Method, Protocol and Path, choose the Body type (form for bodies like a=1&b=2), and paste the body as the Body template. In the body, replace the message you typed with {text}, and the password, if it appears, with {password}.
  6. Set Sign-in (none, basic or digest), the User name and the Clock password. The password is stored encrypted.

Other placeholders you can use: {plain_text} (the message without colour commands), {xml} (an AND XML message with priority and display time), {color}, {seconds}, {priority} and {flashers}. Saving the delivery setup again replaces it.

Until delivery is set up, messages are kept but not sent.

3. Add the clocks

In Clocks, choose Add for each clock: a Name, its Address (IP address or host name, optionally with :port), a Group such as the building, and the Model. Veyra checks every few minutes whether each clock is reachable and shows it in the Reachable column.

Send a message

In Clock Messages, choose Add:

FieldWhat to enter
MessageUp to 1,000 characters.
Send toBlank or all for every clock, or the name of a group or of one clock.
ColourThe text colour.
Show for (seconds)Default 60. 0 keeps the message until another one replaces it.
Prioritynormal, high or emergency. A clock showing a higher-priority message ignores lower ones until it ends.
FlashersFor clocks with flasher lights.
Send atBlank sends now. Or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM in the organization's time zone.

The list shows each message with its Status and Result. Deleting a scheduled message cancels it. A scheduled message that could not be sent within an hour of its time (for example, the server was down) is logged as not sent rather than shown late.

Send a short test message to one clock first.

Messages with the bells

In Clock Bell Messages, choose Add to show text whenever a bell schedule rings:

  • Bell schedule: the schedule's name, or * for every schedule.
  • Text: {summary} (the default) is the calendar event's name, such as Period 2.
  • Send to, Colour and Show for (seconds) as for messages.

If messages do not appear

  • Reachable shows a problem: check the address and that the server can reach the clock's network.
  • The result shows an error from the clock: compare the Clock Delivery setup with a new capture from the clock's web page, especially the path and the sign-in.
  • Colour codes appear as text: turn on the inline text commands setting on the clock.

guides.title: Manage voicemail boxes and shared inboxes
guides.summary: Give extensions a voicemail box, set PINs and email delivery, and create shared inboxes that several phones watch.

headings.title: Create a box for an extension

guides.html:
Every extension can have one voicemail box. Callers reach it when the phone is not answered, is busy or is on Do Not Disturb, and from inbound routes and phone-menu keys that point at it. You can also create shared inboxes: boxes with their own number that belong to no single phone, such as an Attendance line that several office phones watch.

Voicemail boxes are listed under Telephony → Voicemail.

Before you start

  • For new messages to be emailed, an SMTP server must be set up on the Email delivery card under Settings. Until then, the Voicemail page shows Email delivery is not configured and messages stay in the boxes.
  • You need permission to change voicemail (voicemail.write).

Create a box for an extension

  1. Choose New voicemail box.
  2. Pick the Extension. Only extensions without a box are offered.
  3. PIN: 4 to 10 digits, or leave it empty for a random PIN.
  4. Ring time (seconds): how long the phone rings before voicemail answers, 5 to 120 (default 20).
  5. Use the extension user's email address: on by default. New messages go to the email address of the person the extension belongs to. Untick it to enter another address under Email address for new messages, or leave that empty to keep messages in the box only.
  6. Choose Create box.
  7. The PIN is shown once. Copy it and give it to the user now.
  8. Use Deploy changes in the top bar so the phone system learns the box.

You can also create a box from the extension's own page.

If the extension follows an extension template, the template may set or lock some voicemail options. Locked options can only be changed in the template.

Box options

When you create or edit a box (click its row), these options are available:

OptionWhat it does
Operator extension (press 0)A caller who presses 0 during the greeting rings this extension. Empty: 0 does nothing.
After-hours greetingChoose a time condition: while it is closed, the box plays its After hours greeting instead of the Unavailable one. Needs a deployment.
Press 1 during the greeting / Press 2 during the greetingDoes nothing, Tries the follow-me numbers (key 1 of an extension's box only), or Rings another number (an extension, ring group or queue). Users can set these themselves too.
Attach the recording to the emailOn by default. Off: the email only says a message arrived.
Delete the message from the box once it has been emailedSaves storage. The message is deleted only after the email server accepted it; if sending fails, it stays. Needs an email address and the recording attached.
Delete messages older than (days)1 to 3650. Once a day, older messages are deleted from every folder of the box. Empty keeps them.
EnabledA disabled box keeps its settings and messages, but calls no longer land in it.

Each message can be up to 3 minutes long, and greetings up to 60 seconds.

Reset a PIN

Open the box and choose Reset PIN. A new random PIN is shown once. The old PIN stops working at the next deployment. Users can also change their PIN from the phone (*97, mailbox options) or on their account page, except for a shared inbox, whose PIN only an administrator resets here.

Shared inboxes

A shared inbox has its own number and is not tied to one phone. Callers reach it by dialling its number, or through inbound routes and phone-menu keys that point at it. The phones you list as members light their message lamp when it has new messages, and their users see it on My Phone.

  1. Choose New shared inbox.
  2. Enter a Name (for example Attendance line) and a Number from the numbering plan.
  3. Add Member phones.
  4. Set the PIN and an Email address for new messages, for example a shared office mailbox.
  5. Choose Create box, note the PIN, and deploy the changes.

From a phone, members open the inbox with *98: enter the inbox's number, then its PIN. Dialling the inbox's number itself leaves a message.

Point an inbound route or a phone-menu key at the shared inbox, for example press 1 to report an absence.

Listen to a box's messages

Messages on a box's row opens its messages and greetings, as the user sees them:

  • Messages: play, Move to another folder, Forward a copy to another box, Email it to an address (it stays in the box unless you tick Delete it from the voicemail box once the email is sent), or Delete it. Folders are New, Old, Work, Family, Friends and Urgent.
  • Greetings: play, Upload or Record in the browser, or Remove each greeting: Unavailable, Busy, Name, Temporary, Extended absence and After hours. Below them is the box's Extended absence (see Your voicemail).

Listening to a message and every change are written to the audit log.

Extended absence for many boxes

For a break when nobody answers, such as the summer, set one absence for many boxes at once:

  1. Choose Extended absence… at the top of the page.
  2. Leave Extended absence on switched on.
  3. Set the First day (empty: from now) and the Last day (empty: until it is turned off). After the last day it turns itself off.
  4. Tick Take no messages while away if callers should hear the greeting and then be hung up on, without leaving a message.
  5. Pick the boxes: tick them one by one, or narrow the list with Organization or Find a box and choose Pick all … shown.
  6. Choose Set for … boxes.

Callers hear each box's Extended absence greeting (or its Temporary greeting) for these dates. It takes effect at once; no deployment is needed. To end it early, open the dialog again, switch Extended absence on off, pick the boxes and choose Turn off for ….

Delete a box

Open the box and choose Delete box. Routes and phone-menu keys that point at it must be changed first. Then deploy the changes.

If something doesn't work

  • No emails arrive: check the Email delivery card under Settings, and the box's email address. Look in the recipient's spam folder.
  • The user's PIN does not work: PIN changes reach the phone system at the next deployment. Check that changes have been deployed.
  • The Messages tab says messages are not available on this server: Veyra cannot reach the phone system's voicemail storage on this server. Check System → Health.

guides.title: Set up fax
guides.summary: Receive faxes as PDFs by email, let staff send PDFs as faxes from My Phone, and connect fax machines through an analog adapter.

headings.title: Fax machines on an analog adapter

guides.html:
Veyra handles fax in three ways:

  • Receiving: a fax number of yours answers as a fax inbox. The pages arrive by email as a PDF.
  • Sending from the browser: staff send a PDF as a fax from the Fax widget on My Phone. No fax machine needed.
  • Fax machines: an existing fax machine plugs into an analog telephone adapter (ATA) port and works like any extension.

Everything is managed under Telephony → Fax.

Before you start

  • Fax emails need an SMTP server on the Email delivery card under Settings.
  • Set the organization's Fax header (the line printed at the top of sent pages) and Fax station ID (the number announced to the other machine) on the organization's page under Organizations. Inboxes can override them.
  • Fax travels over your SIP trunk. If your carrier supports T.38 fax relay, turn on Fax over T.38 on the trunk; otherwise faxes travel as audio, which works with most carriers.

Receive faxes by email

  1. Choose New fax inbox.
  2. Enter a Name, for example Front office.
  3. Under Email the PDF to, enter up to 20 addresses, one per line.
  4. Optionally set a Station ID (digits, + and spaces) and a Page header (up to 64 characters). Empty uses the organization's.
  5. Choose Create inbox.
  6. Point your fax number at it: on the DID or the inbound route, choose the destination Fax to email and this inbox.
  7. Use Deploy changes in the top bar.

A fax that arrives is converted to a PDF, emailed to the recipients and listed under Faxes. An inbox with no recipients shows No recipients: its faxes are only listed. A disabled inbox is kept, but the routes pointing at it stop receiving.

Sending from My Phone

Users with an extension see the Fax widget on My Phone: they enter the Fax number, pick a PDF to send (up to 20 MB and 50 pages), optionally Add a cover sheet, and choose Send fax. The fax goes out with the extension's outbound caller ID, and the user is emailed when it is delivered or fails. See Your phone at a glance: My Phone.

  • Veyra tries up to 3 times when the line is busy or does not answer, a few minutes apart.
  • To stop some phones from sending faxes, untick May send faxes from My Phone in their class of service.
  • The server needs Ghostscript to convert PDFs; if it is missing, sending answers Fax unavailable.

Follow faxes

The Faxes card lists sent and received faxes, newest first, with filters for direction and state (Waiting, Dialling, Sending, Sent, Failed, Received, Cancelled). The list refreshes by itself while faxes are on their way. Administrators who can manage fax can:

  • download a fax as PDF,
  • Cancel a fax that is still waiting or in progress,
  • Retry a failed or cancelled send.

Faxes and their files are kept for 90 days by default; a platform administrator can change that on the Retention card under Settings. A fax whose file was removed can no longer be retried.

Fax machines on an analog adapter

Connect the fax machine to a port of an analog telephone adapter (ATA) and give that port its own extension, like any phone. On the extension's page, the Fax machine (T.38) switch decides how faxes travel:

  • On: Veyra offers T.38 to the adapter, so faxes are relayed end to end. Use it when the trunk has Fax over T.38 turned on. Set the adapter's fax mode to T.38 as well.
  • Off (default): the fax travels as ordinary audio (G.711). This works with any trunk; set the adapter's fax mode to pass-through.

The change needs a deployment.

If something doesn't work

  • Faxes fail with errors part-way through: try the other setting of Fax machine (T.38) or Fax over T.38 on the trunk, matching what your carrier supports.
  • No email for received faxes: check the inbox's recipients and the Email delivery settings.
  • "Fax not allowed": the user's class of service does not allow sending faxes.
  • "No phone": faxes are sent with the user's extension's caller ID; the user has no extension.

guides.title: Set up single sign-on
guides.summary: Let people sign in to Veyra with their Google Workspace, Microsoft 365 or other work account.
guides.html:
With single sign-on, people sign in to Veyra, and to the Companion extension, with the account their school or company already gives them. There is no separate Veyra password to remember. Veyra checks the provider's signature on every sign-in and keeps no access to the account.

Veyra works with Google Workspace, Microsoft Entra ID (Microsoft 365) and any other OpenID Connect provider, such as Okta, Keycloak or Authentik.

Open System → Sign-in and choose Set up a provider. The guided setup has five steps.

Before you start

  • You need to be an administrator in Veyra who can manage sign-in.
  • You need administrator access to your provider: a Google Workspace super administrator, or a Microsoft Entra Application Administrator.
  • Keep the Veyra setup open in one tab and the provider's console in another.

1. Choose the provider

Pick the kind of account people already have.

2. Register Veyra with the provider

The guide shows the exact steps for your provider, with links into its console. It also shows the redirect address to copy, which is unique to this server.

  • Google: in the Google Cloud console, create an Internal app and a Web application OAuth client. Paste the redirect address under Authorized redirect URIs. Copy the client ID and the client secret right away, because Google shows the secret only once.
  • Microsoft: in the Entra admin center, create a single-tenant app registration. Paste the redirect address as a Web redirect URI. Note the Application (client) ID and the Directory (tenant) ID, then create a client secret and copy its Value, not its Secret ID.
Microsoft client secrets expire after at most 24 months. Put a reminder in your calendar to create a new one and enter it in Veyra (Edit on the Sign-in page) before it runs out. Otherwise single sign-on stops working.

3. Enter the credentials

Paste the client ID and secret (and, for Microsoft, the tenant ID). Then fill in:

  • Allowed e-mail domains: only accounts with these addresses can sign in, for example example.org. Personal Gmail and Outlook accounts are always refused.
  • Button name: the text people see, as in Sign in with Google.

The secret is stored encrypted and is never shown again.

4. Choose who can sign in

People who already have a Veyra account with the same e-mail address are linked to it the first time they sign in.

  • Create accounts on first sign-in off: only people who already have a Veyra account can sign in.
  • On: anyone in the allowed domains gets an account the first time, with the role you choose (usually Standard user, which gives access to their own phone and voicemail).

Save and test saves the provider turned off, so nobody sees its button yet.

5. Test and turn on

  1. Veyra first checks that it can reach the provider.
  2. Choose Test sign-in and sign in with a real account, exactly as people will. Veyra shows which account the sign-in would use, or why it would be refused, with a hint for the usual mistakes (wrong secret, redirect address, domain). The test signs no one in and changes nothing.
  3. When the test works, choose Turn on the sign-in button. The button now appears on the Veyra sign-in page.

You can test again at any time with Test on the provider's row.

Good to know

  • The recovery administrator created at installation always signs in with a password, so you can never be locked out by a provider problem.
  • To let the Companion sign in by itself on managed Chromebooks, see Roll out the Companion extension.

guides.title: Firewall and bans
guides.summary: Ban attackers automatically, keep your own phones and networks on the allow list so they are never locked out, and recover from the console.

headings.title: Limit who can reach each service
Locked out? Recover from the console

guides.html:
A phone system that can be reached from the internet is attacked within hours: robots try extension numbers and passwords to make expensive calls. Veyra's firewall watches for that and bans the addresses that misbehave.

The firewall is off after installation. Open System → Firewall.

Anyone who may view the firewall sees its bans, events, lists and settings. Only people who may also change it (the permission Change firewall rules, bans and settings) see Allow, Block, Lift, Block permanently, Add feed, the feed and list buttons, and Save settings. Without it, the Settings tab says You can view these settings; changing them needs the firewall write permission.

How it works

  • Every suspicious event (a wrong SIP password, an unknown extension, a failed sign-in) scores points against the address it came from.
  • An address that reaches the Score that bans within the Window is banned for a while. A repeat offender gets a longer ban each time, up to the Longest ban.
  • Addresses on the allow list are never banned or blocked, whatever they do.
  • Addresses on the block list are always dropped, unless they are also allowed.

1. Fill the allow list first

Your phones, trunks and administrators must never be locked out. Before turning the firewall on, open the Allow and block tab.

Some entries are added and kept up to date by Veyra itself, marked by their Source:

  • This server,
  • Local network: the networks listed under Local networks in the SIP settings (System → Telephony Engine),
  • Trunk: the addresses of your phone providers.

Add the rest with Allow:

  1. Enter the Address or network, such as 203.0.113.7 or 10.20.0.0/16.
  2. Add a Comment (why, for whom).
  3. Choose when it Expires (Never, or 1 hour to 30 days).

Add every network your phones live on (voice VLANs, other buildings, the VPN), your offices and administrators' networks, and remote workers with fixed addresses.

If a whole building's phones sit behind one router, one misconfigured phone there can get that address banned, and every phone behind it with it. Put such addresses on the allow list.

2. Turn it on

On the Settings tab, switch Firewall on, then Save settings and confirm Turn on. If the address you are using is not on the allow list, the page warns Your address is not on the allow list.

Limit who can reach each service

Under Who may reach each service, each of SIP signaling, Call audio (RTP), Web interface and provisioning and SSH can be open to Anyone not banned or blocked or to Only the allow list. Set the SSH ports if SSH is not on port 22.

Limiting a service is safe to try: after saving, the page shows Keep the new restrictions? with a countdown. Choose Keep these settings within 60 seconds. If you have locked yourself out, you cannot press it, and the change is undone by itself.

Automatic bans

Under Automatic bans: Score that bans (default 10), Window (minutes) (default 10), First ban (minutes) (default 60) and Longest ban (days) (default 7). Points per event sets how much each kind of event counts, such as Wrong SIP password, Unknown SIP account or Failed sign-in. Set a kind to 0 to ignore it.

See what happens

  • Overview: whether the firewall is on, Active bans, Suspicious events (24 h), Bans (24 h), and the Most active addresses (24 h). Click an address to see its events.
  • Bans: active, past or all bans, with the reason and until when. Lift ends a ban now. Block permanently moves the address to the block list.
  • Events: every suspicious event, filtered by address or source (Phone system, Sign-in, Provisioning, Web server). Tick Only allowed addresses that would have been banned to find allowed addresses that misbehave, such as a phone with an old password.

Block an address or network

On Allow and block, choose Block. Enter the Address or network, a Comment, and optionally tick Services to block only some (none ticked blocks everything), and when it Expires.

Blocklist feeds (optional)

Under Settings → Blocklist feeds, Add feed to drop addresses that others have already seen attacking:

  • Address list (one per line, HTTPS): a public list, such as Spamhaus DROP.
  • CrowdSec local API (bouncer): if you run CrowdSec, its address and a Bouncer key (create one with sudo cscli bouncers add veyra).

Feeds are refreshed every 10 minutes. The allow list still wins.

Phone bootstrap networks

A brand-new phone fetches the Veyra certificate over plain HTTP before it can use HTTPS. Phone bootstrap networks limits that to the networks you list, such as your staging or voice VLAN. Empty means the Local networks of the SIP settings.

Locked out? Recover from the console

On the server's console (or over SSH, if SSH still works), run:

sudo veyra firewall off

It turns the firewall off and removes its rules at once. Fix the allow list, then turn it on again. sudo veyra firewall status shows the settings and the active bans.

When it does not work

  • The firewall service is not running: rules already applied stay, but nothing new is banned. Check journalctl -u veyra-firewall on the server.
  • Some event sources cannot be read: Veyra cannot read the engine's security log or the web server's log, so it cannot see those attacks.
  • The Many firewall bans alert: see Health, alerts and diagnostics.

guides.title: Get a public HTTPS certificate (Let's Encrypt)
guides.summary: Get a free certificate that every browser trusts, so nobody has to install the Veyra certificate and passkeys and the Companion work.

headings.title: Go back to the Veyra certificate

guides.html:
Out of the box, Veyra uses a certificate from its own certificate authority (the Veyra CA). Phones Veyra sets up trust it, but browsers warn until the Veyra CA certificate is installed on each computer.

A public certificate from Let's Encrypt (free) or another authority fixes that: every browser trusts it with nothing installed. Passkeys and the Companion extension need one, or the Veyra CA on every computer.

Phones are not affected: they keep using the Veyra certificate, which also keeps answering the server's IP addresses and every other name.

You need to be a platform administrator. Open System → Settings and find the HTTPS certificate card. Its badge says Veyra CA only or Public, n days left.

Before you start

  • A host name people will use, such as pbx.example.org, in a domain you control. Not an IP address.
  • A way to prove you own it. Choose one:
    • DNS record: Veyra adds a temporary record in your DNS. Works even when the server cannot be reached from the internet, which is usual for a phone system. You need an API key for your DNS provider.
    • Web request on port 80: the authority connects to the name on port 80. The name must point (in public DNS) at an address whose port 80 is forwarded to this server.

1. Fill in the settings

  • Host names: the names users type in the browser, separated by commas. A wildcard (*.example.org) needs the DNS check.
  • Email for expiry notices: the authority writes here if renewal keeps failing.
  • How the authority checks you own the name: DNS record or Web request on port 80.
  • For DNS, the DNS provider that hosts the name: Cloudflare, Amazon Route 53, Google Cloud DNS, DigitalOcean, Linode (Akamai), DNSimple, OVH, or Your own DNS server (RFC 2136: BIND, Windows DNS with TSIG). Then the provider's credentials, and Wait for the DNS record (seconds). Give the key the narrowest rights the provider offers (edit DNS of this zone only). It is stored encrypted and never shown again.
  • Certificate authority: Let's Encrypt, Let's Encrypt staging (test the setup; browsers do not trust it), or Another ACME authority (with its ACME directory address, and the External account key ID and External account HMAC key if it asks for them, as ZeroSSL and Sectigo do).

Choose Save settings. If something is missing, the card says what.

Try Let's Encrypt staging first. It has generous limits, so mistakes cost nothing. When it works, switch to Let's Encrypt, save, and get the real certificate.

2. Get the certificate

Choose Get the certificate…, check the names, and choose Get it now. It takes up to a few minutes; Show output shows the progress. When it is done, the card shows the certificate In use, who issued it and until when. Calls are not affected.

If the firewall limits the web interface to the allow list, Veyra opens port 80 to everyone for ten minutes while the authority checks.

Renewal

Veyra checks every day and renews the certificate when 30 days or fewer are left. Renew now does the same check at once (it renews only within those 30 days). Get a new certificate… gets a fresh one regardless, for example after changing the names.

If a renewal fails, the Public certificate not renewed alert is raised (see Health, alerts and diagnostics).

Go back to the Veyra certificate

Stop using it… gives every name the Veyra certificate again. Browsers without the Veyra CA installed will warn again, and passkeys stop working until they trust it. The stored DNS credentials are deleted.

From the server console

  • sudo veyra certificate status shows the certificate in use and the last run.
  • sudo veyra certificate renew renews now if 30 days or fewer are left.
  • sudo veyra certificate remove goes back to the Veyra certificate.

Getting the first certificate needs the web page, where the settings are entered.

When it does not work

Open Show output and read the last lines.

  • DNS check fails: the API key lacks rights to the zone, or the record had not spread yet. Raise Wait for the DNS record (seconds).
  • Port 80 check fails: the name does not point to your public address, or port 80 is not forwarded to this server.
  • Too many requests: Let's Encrypt limits how often you can ask. Wait, and use staging while testing.

guides.title: Audit log
guides.summary: Find out who changed what, who signed in, and which attempts were refused.
guides.html:
System → Audit Log is a lasting record of administrative actions, sign-ins and refused attempts. Entries cannot be edited or deleted, not even by a platform administrator; only the retention period (below) removes old ones.

Use it to answer questions such as who changed this ring group?, who downloaded that packet capture? or is someone trying passwords?

Read the list

The newest events are first, 50 per page. Each row shows:

  • Time
  • Action: what happened, as a short code such as extension.create, auth.login or updates.approve.
  • Actor: who did it: a person, an integration token, the system, or cli (<name>) for a command run on the server console.
  • Target: what it was done to.
  • Outcome: success, failure or denied (the person was not allowed).

Find something

  • Search action or actor: type part of an action (such as firewall or backup) or a person's name or email.
  • The outcome filter shows only Success, Failure or Denied events. Denied and Failure together are a quick way to spot someone trying things they should not.
  • The two date fields, From and To, limit the list to whole days: from the start of the first day to the end of the last. Leave either empty for no limit.

Export the list

Choose Export CSV at the top of the page. The file holds the events that match the search, outcome and dates you set, newest first, up to 100,000 events. Each row has the time, actor, organization, action, target, outcome, IP address, request ID and details.

See the details

Click a row. The panel shows the Time, Outcome, Actor (and whether it was a user, a token or the system), Target, Organization, the IP address the request came from, the Request ID, and the Details: what changed, as the system recorded it.

Who sees what

You need permission to read the audit log. Organization administrators see the events of their organizations; platform administrators see everything, including events that belong to no organization (such as server settings).

How long entries are kept

By default two years. A platform administrator can change it on the Retention card under System → Settings, but never below one year.

guides.title: Roll out the Companion extension
guides.summary: Put the Veyra Companion in people's Chrome or Edge browsers by policy, with the server address filled in.

headings.title: 1. Choose where the browsers are managed
2. Make the browsers trust this server

guides.html:
The Veyra Companion is a browser extension for Chrome and Edge. People use it to call any number from their desk phone with one click, look people up, see who is calling and listen to voicemail. See Use the Companion extension for what it does for them.

This guide is for the administrator who installs it for everyone. The same steps are in Veyra at System → Companion rollout, with this server's values filled in and buttons to copy them.

Before you start

  • You need to be a platform administrator in Veyra.
  • You need administrator access to whatever manages the browsers: the Google Admin console, Group Policy, or Intune.
  • Try everything on one test computer or Chromebook first, in a test group or organizational unit.

1. Choose where the browsers are managed

OptionUse it for
Google Admin consoleChromebooks, and Chrome on Windows or Mac enrolled in Chrome Browser Cloud Management
Windows: Group Policy or IntuneChrome and Edge on computers joined to Active Directory, or joined to Microsoft Entra and managed by Intune
People install it themselvesBrowsers nobody manages

If you have several kinds of computers, go through the guide once for each.

Chrome and Edge install extensions from outside their stores only on managed computers. On a computer nobody manages, the browser ignores the policy and the person has to load the extension by hand.

2. Make the browsers trust this server

The extension talks to Veyra over HTTPS. Unlike a person, it cannot click past a certificate warning.

  • If Veyra has a public certificate for the address people use (for example from Let's Encrypt, under Settings → HTTPS certificate), every browser already trusts it. The guide in Veyra says Nothing to do and you can go on.
  • Otherwise Veyra uses a certificate signed by its own certificate authority. Download the Veyra CA certificate from the guide and push it to the browsers first:
    • Google Admin console: Devices → Networks → Certificates → Add certificate. Upload veyra-ca.crt and tick Chromebook and Chrome browser under Certificate authority.
    • Group Policy: Computer Configuration → Policies → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Public Key Policies → Trusted Root Certification Authorities → Import.
    • Intune: Devices → Configuration → Create → Windows 10 and later → Templates → Trusted certificate. Use the destination store Computer certificate store - Root.

To check, open the Veyra address on the test computer. There should be no warning.

A public certificate is often easier than pushing the Veyra CA. Nothing has to be installed on any computer, and phones keep using the Veyra CA as before.

3. Choose how people sign in

  • E-mail and password: people sign in with their Veyra account and their second factor if they have one.
  • Single sign-on: if you have set up single sign-on, choose the provider. The extension then shows a Sign in with Google (or Microsoft) button. On managed Chromebooks it signs in by itself, once Veyra's OAuth client is marked Trusted in the Google Admin console (Security → Access and data control → API controls → Manage third-party app access).

4. Push the extension

The guide shows three values: the extension ID, the update URL, and the install line (the two joined with a semicolon).

Google Admin console

  1. Devices → Chrome → Apps & extensions → Users & browsers, and pick the organizational unit.
  2. The yellow + button → Add Chrome app or extension by ID → From a custom URL. Paste the extension ID and the update URL.
  3. Set Installation policy to Force install + pin to browser toolbar.
